Retain the first Fourier harmonic for analytic slow-roll predictions of curvature perturbations, spectral index, tensor ratio and non-Gaussianity. Compare these estimates with numerical results in Table 1.
Evaluate the one-loop potential from gauge, ghost and scalar self-interactions. Add a constant so that V(0)=0; this normalization does not constitute a solution of the cosmological constant problem.
Estimate gravitational decay using Γgrav∼mφ³/MPl² and mφ²∼V″, compare the decay rate with the end-of-inflation Hubble scale, and infer a reheating-temperature upper estimate.

Compute the spectrum using one-loop, two-stage match-and-run evolution, tree-level matching at the heavy-particle scale and finite one-loop thresholds. Precision unification uses two-loop gauge running and a parameter scan accounting for spectrum–coupling feedback.

Use the nonperturbative hidden-sector superpotential and assumed Kähler potential to minimize the supergravity potential and evaluate F-terms and soft parameters. A large hidden-cycle volume permits a semi-analytic inverse-volume expansion.

Expand the ADM action to quadratic order in field perturbations in spatially flat gauge. Solve the lapse and shift constraints at first order and substitute them into the action; the shift drops out after integration by parts.

Regroup field-metric derivatives into covariant derivatives and Riemann-curvature terms. Project onto a moving orthonormal adiabatic/entropy basis, then canonically normalize the two-field modes for conformal-time quantization.

Vacuum-decay estimates use semiclassical instanton rates, sums over channels and a dilute-gas-like multi-instanton model. Flux-transition estimates use supergravity extrema and domain-wall tension related to a central function.

Black-hole formation/evaporation thought experiments load distinct species into a hole and demand their subsequent release. Localization sets the minimum energy added per particle; integrating these increments estimates how many species can participate before horizon-size or evaporation-time restrictions intervene.

Use the Hawking–Horowitz background-subtracted extrinsic-curvature mass and imported holographic-renormalization formulas for cascading geometries to extract energy and operator VEVs. A DBI plus Chern–Simons probe calculation examines the resulting D3-brane force.

Solve homogeneous linearized IIB equations in the ultraviolet with radial metric, dilaton and flux functions. The retained asymptotic terms are 1/r⁴ and log(r)/r⁴; radial coordinate freedom fixes part of the metric ansatz. Source terms and conserved charges motivate identification with brane/antibrane states.

Represent D-branes by coherent closed-string boundary states and orientifold planes by crosscap states. Their overlaps with a closed-string propagator encode cylinder, Möbius-strip and Klein-bottle amplitudes; low-energy Einstein-frame brane couplings fix the tadpole normalization and motivate contact vertices.

Insert a brane bounce operator representing a two-point closed-string contact interaction. Summing repeated insertions gives a geometric-series propagator; higher-point brane contact interactions are then joined using these resummed legs, with diagram symmetry factors included.

For the orientifold system, include both brane and O-plane bounces. Separate large-proper-time divergences into a tachyon part Δ_T and a massless part Δ, tracking their different signs in boundary–boundary and boundary–crosscap overlaps.

Locate marginally stable modes along selected parameter curves rather than construct the nonlinear condensed phase. For m²>0 require ψ→0 at infinity; for negative m² use the AdS source-free boundary condition associated with a selected operator dimension.

Study static, infinitesimal scalar perturbations through a radial boundary-value problem on the fixed charged background. Horizon regularity removes the logarithmic solution; linearity permits setting the regular horizon amplitude to one while its physical amplitude remains infinitesimal.

Wrapped-brane supersymmetry is determined using κ-symmetry and calibration conditions. A separate DBI plus Wess–Zumino calculation gives the reported cancellation of radial forces for the displayed D4 configuration.

Holomorphic torus curves are represented using Weierstrass functions and two additional polynomial equations. Bézout and Bernstein counting relate polynomial degrees to wrapping numbers; Bernstein's mixed volume bounds finitely many roots in (C*)^n and is attained for generic coefficients. Polynomial coefficients and Wilson-line directions estimate branch dimensions.

Bulk supersymmetry is analyzed through SU(3)-structure pure spinors, a Clifford map between bispinors and forms, and flux-dependent supersymmetry equations. The paper solves these equations for the background spinors and stabilized moduli.

Impose constant scalar equation of state and ρφ∝a^{-3(1+ωφ)} in a fluid-dominated background. Integrate the resulting field evolution, then use the DBI field equation to determine the tension and potential for the constant-γ branch.

Transform to logarithmic time and dimensionless deviations from the exact scaling solution, then linearize an autonomous system to study local stability. Numerical cosmological evolution follows different initial conditions into the regime where the scalar is no longer a test field.

Expand the N = 1 F-term potential and inverse Kähler metric to first order in the proposed instanton correction, then retain leading volume powers. Derivatives of the corrected metric involve all chiral fields, even when heavy fields obey supersymmetric stabilization conditions.

Use imported semiclassical NS5 corrections to the universal-hypermultiplet metric, expressed through the Przanowski master-equation framework. Gauge a surviving isometry, calculate its norm and moment-map contributions, and match an N = 1 truncation to a corrected Kähler potential and chiral coordinate.

Reviewed tools include solving constrained superspace Bianchi identities off shell, chiral densities and projectors for invariant actions, and gauge completion to identify component fields by matching superspace and spacetime transformation laws.

The R^4 analysis uses constrained superspace variations and component expansions with differential constraints and derivative commutators. The black-hole discussion imports Wald/Sen entropy methods: auxiliary fields enter the near-horizon entropy function as independent off-shell variables before extremization.
Translate BRST operators into cohomology, count scalar and vector zero modes, insert the obstruction class when necessary, and integrate on the classical or instanton moduli space.
Compute central charges, compare subgroup characters with the E8 character, and realize the additional conformal families as finite-orbifold twisted sectors.

Replace left-moving fermions by WZW fibers, couple their chiral multiplication to the pulled-back target connection, and cancel gauge and supersymmetry variations through the B field and right-moving anomaly.
Lift bundle data and operator classes to instanton moduli, saturate excess modes, and use anomaly constraints plus GRR to obtain a top-form integral.
Expand fields into worldsheet sections, quotient bosonic coefficients by the GLSM gauge action, and assemble charged fermionic coefficients into the induced bundle.
Use the GLSM Coulomb branch or an A-twisted heterotic Landau-Ginzburg model as an alternative computational description. Full-moduli comparisons require an explicit change of fields.
Use left- and right-moving zero-mode counts to select insertions, multiply their sheaf-cohomology representatives, and integrate after identifying the determinant bundle with the canonical bundle.
Apply the cited spectral-cover construction to stable SU(5) bundles, select generic full-holonomy connections, and combine two copies through the Z5 quotient.

The authors analyze the SUGRA scalar potential and the covariant mass matrix on curved field space. Numerical integration follows the coupled fields and compares slow-roll parameters projected along the trajectory with the usual potential-based quantities.

A Taylor expansion about the post-inflationary modulus minimum and minimization over its displacement gives the leading correction δV=−Σ_A(∂_A V_mix)^2/[2∂_A^2 V_mod], A=σ,γ. The negative sign reflects the modulus adjusting to lower the total energy.

For large uniform sources, bulk charge neutrality and energy minimization determine s_0 and ω_0, with 2q²ω_0s_0²=ρ and q²ω_0²=m²+εs_0². Finite-source and laboratory estimates use screening lengths, thin-shell arguments, dimensional analysis and finite-conductivity Casimir reasoning.

Energy minimization for a charged sphere compares unscreened vector-field energy with scalar-condensate energy. Static profiles satisfy coupled nonlinear equations: ∇²|s|=(m²+ε|s|²−q²ω²)|s| and ∇²ω=−g²ρ+2q²g²ω|s|².

Construct the four-dimensional N=1 supergravity potential using K(S)=−ln(S+S̄), K(T)=−3ln(T+T̄) and W=MP³(C−A exp(−a0 S)). Use its no-scale structure, expand near a dilaton minimum, and lift the approximate potential to ten-dimensional Einstein variables.

Derive the coupled dilaton and internal Einstein equations, identify a common fixed point, and linearize in δb and δφ. The stability calculation treats the fluctuations as coupled oscillators with an exp(iωt) ansatz and drops Hubble damping on the stated grounds that it stabilizes the motion.

Uses a one-loop effective potential consisting of the tree-level supergravity potential, a temperature-independent Coleman-Weinberg contribution, and thermal bosonic/fermionic integrals. High-temperature mass-trace expansions treat light modes; Boltzmann-suppressed low-temperature expansions treat heavy quarks near the supersymmetric vacua.

Finds the quark instability from a zero eigenvalue of the thermal plus classical squared-mass matrix. Computes meson displacement by linearizing the supergravity thermal extremum equation. Searches numerically for modulus destabilization using simultaneous vanishing of its first and second potential derivatives.

Completes the Yang–Mills action into a duality square plus a topological term. Constructs solutions using a sigma-matrix ansatz proportional to a derivative of ln φ, with the Bianchi identity connecting selfduality to the field equations.
Uses WKB and bounce fluctuation analysis for tunnelling and instability; applies Derrick scaling and constrained variational problems to Higgs-coupled instantons.

Relates linearized duality and background-gauge constraints to the Dirac index. Uses zero-mode inner products as a collective-coordinate metric and Jacobian, then integrates orthogonal fluctuations through determinants with zero eigenvalues excluded.

Uses warp-weighted averages ⟨Q⟩A=(∫M QeᴬΩ√f)/(∫M eᴬΩ√f), splitting each function into an averaged mode and a zero-average fluctuation. Nonnegative averaging weights allow a negative averaged energy-condition probe to establish violation somewhere on the internal space.

The optimal solution minimizes the evolution inequality's right-hand side and saturates the constraints, maximizing allowed e-foldings. At constant w, v=tξ0|A satisfies a Riccati equation t dv/dt=α2v²+α1v+α0 with endpoints ±vF; root positions determine whether traversal takes finite time.

Constructs stress-tensor scalar probes for large-space and internal directions, substitutes the higher-dimensional Einstein equations, and derives an evolution inequality for the averaged internal expansion ξ0|A plus an algebraic bound on ξ0|A². An optimizing averaging parameter controls fluctuation, shear, and warp-gradient contributions.

Normalized averages use weight e^{AΩ} times the internal volume measure; A=2 is canonical. Optimizing A controls deformation and warp terms, reducing duration bounds to differential inequalities for the averaged volume velocity.

Oxidation reverses dimensional reduction: prescribe the lower-dimensional cosmology, parameterize compatible internal evolution, and use the higher-dimensional Einstein tensor to constrain the required stress-energy.

Negative trace combinations provide sufficient tests for NEC violation. For curved spaces, curvature-independent stress combinations isolate the SEC; the duration calculation also uses the NEC combination ρᴰ+P₃ᴰ to bound initial and final velocities.

Expand the action to quadratic order in h₁₂, Fourier transform as e^{−iωt+iqx₃}, and obtain its radial wave equation. The retarded stress-tensor correlator gives η in the small-frequency, small-momentum limit.

Geometrical optics identifies high-momentum graviton trajectories with null geodesics of an effective metric. Conserved ω and q reduce radial motion to a particle with energy α²=(ω/q)² in potential c_g².

Transform the wave equation to Schrödinger form, identify metastable states, and use WKB with Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization. Differentiating the quantization condition at fixed level relates quasiparticle group velocity to boundary geodesic displacement divided by travel time.

Obtain BPS equations from four-dimensional F- and D-flatness. Determine representations by branching the enhanced adjoint, and count zero modes using bundle-valued Dolbeault cohomology, Hodge theory, Serre duality and index formulas on surfaces and curves.

Use the bulk holomorphic F-term −∫S Tr(F^(0,2)∧Φ) and supersymmetric defect couplings. Defect condensation sources ∂̄Aϕ=δΣ⟪σc,σ⟫, allowing meromorphic ϕ with poles along Σ. Compare its invariant polynomials with the bundle assignments and parameters of geometric singularity unfoldings.

A spherical-harmonic expansion shows that higher multipoles increase the Newtonian potential without changing the single-field origin-to-infinity excursion. A fixed-backreaction variational problem then selects a logarithmic radial profile after introducing a short-distance cutoff.

The GR calculation uses the imported Buchdahl scalar exterior and its stated uniqueness properties. Splitting the spherical ADM mass integral into interior and exterior contributions bounds the surface position; maximizing over the exterior parameter β gives the excursion bound.
A complementary heuristic matches oscillating WKB modes inside the sound horizon to frozen curvature perturbations outside it at c_s kη approximately one.
The paper sets subhorizon initial conditions through WKB normalization, solves the mode equation using Bessel functions, and extracts the growing superhorizon solution to determine spectral tilt.

Flux analysis uses harmonic representatives, Hodge decomposition, Lefschetz SU(2), and periods of the holomorphic four-form. The dimensionless GVW superpotential is W = ℓ_M⁻³∫G₄∧Ω₄; its Kähler-covariant derivatives constrain complex structure.

The supplied geometrical toolkit begins with toric varieties as D-flat GLSM quotients by U(1)^s, or corresponding complexified quotients. Divisors, line bundles, linear equivalence, and intersection products provide explicit computational data.

F-theory is constructed operationally from M-theory: reduce along one elliptic-fiber circle, T-dualize along the other, and send fiber area to zero. The fiber modulus becomes the IIB axiodilaton and the limit restores four-dimensional Lorentz invariance.

Expand DBI and Wess–Zumino couplings and propagate NS–NS B₂ and appropriate R–R forms between branes. Use internal-Laplacian eigenfunction Green functions, and boundary-value Green-function equations for the RS and throat examples.

Compute a nonplanar one-loop open-string annulus with gauge vertices on different boundaries, adapting gauge-threshold methods and summing Chan–Paton-weighted stack contributions. In the closed channel, isolate the 1/k² pole from the finite momentum expansion.

Count universal, Wilson-line and charged fermionic zero modes; saturate them with annulus insertions and include annulus/Möbius one-loop determinants. Sum connected distributions of insertions with the appropriate combinatorial factors.

Relate instanton amplitudes to gauge thresholds on fictitious spacetime-filling D5-branes sharing the instanton's internal boundary state. Supersymmetric Ward arguments relate four-fermion absorption amplitudes to second Wilson-line derivatives; integrating relative spacetime positions supplies the threshold measure factor.

Unfold the heterotic modular integral into nondegenerate momentum/winding matrix orbits, organize them as generalized Hecke sums, and identify Type I multiple covers using effective complex structures and modular transformations.

Expand the ten-dimensional action to second order, include the Gibbons–Hawking–York term, integrate internal wavefunctions and impose constraints. Handle five-form self-duality by eliminating half its four-dimensional degrees of freedom and doubling the five-form and Chern–Simons coefficients.

Use axial gauge δgμm=0 and impose Einstein-equation constraints δA=δg̃/8 and ∇̃ⁿ(δg̃mn−g̃mnδg̃/2)=4(∂ⁿ̃A)δg̃mn. The second condition fixes residual internal diffeomorphisms but is imposed by dynamics.

Expand fluctuations in warped generalized Laplace and Lichnerowicz eigenmodes. A Sturm–Liouville argument supplies orthogonality with weight √g̃6 e^{-4A}; scalar reduction motivates simultaneous diagonalization of kinetic and geometric mass terms.

Expand the wrapped D4 DBI action to two derivatives and canonically normalize its position field. The exact field map involves a hypergeometric function; the authors use numerical inversion for the full potential and asymptotic expansions for its quadratic and fractional-power regimes.

Estimate consistency through a Taylor expansion of the moduli potential, dimensional reduction of the brane gravitational field, compact-space source interactions, and curvature/string-loop corrections. These are author estimates of corrections and stability, rather than a complete explicit mass-spectrum calculation.

Use a generalized-calibrated BPS domain wall and the RR Bianchi identity to express its tension as a difference of flux pairings. Matching TDW=2|ΔW| determines the on-shell superpotential; holomorphicity motivates its extension to an off-shell functional.

Read the conformal Kähler potential from the reduced Einstein–Hilbert term, gauge-fix the complex Weyl redundancy, and vary the resulting functionals with respect to polyform holomorphic variables. Add non-perturbative superpotential terms represented by generalized source currents to infer corrected background equations.

Compute zero-spatial-momentum conductivity from an Ax perturbation with e^{-iωt} dependence and ingoing horizon boundary conditions. Use its boundary coefficients for linear response and Kramers–Kronig relations to associate an imaginary pole with a real conductivity delta function.

Numerically integrate the coupled nonlinear radial scalar and electrostatic equations from regular horizon data to the boundary, impose one vanishing scalar coefficient, and fit the resulting condensate curves near the critical temperature.

Kasteleyn signed adjacency matrices, determinants and perfect-matching height functions extract toric data. The characteristic polynomial depends on the reference perfect matching only through overall multiplicative powers of x and y.

Coamoebae and untwisted tilings describe vanishing cycles and their intersections. Directed Fukaya-category compositions are computed through holomorphic-disc counts, corresponding physically to superpotential terms.

NSVZ beta functions and their identically vanishing linear combinations organize marginal couplings. Trial-R a-maximization is compared with Reeb-vector volume minimization; Duistermaat–Heckman localization supplies geometric volume formulas.

For radial flows, solve gravitino and dilatino variations subject to a spinor projection. Supersymmetry expresses fluxes through A, ω and Φ and leaves one differential constraint; selected profiles are integrated using hypergeometric functions. Hitchin flow supplies the geometric G2-lift comparison.

Construct the most general invariant J and Ω, impose their algebraic compatibility and metric positivity, and compute exterior derivatives from reductive-coset structure constants. Read off torsion classes and test the source-modified F2 Bianchi identity and torsion bound.

Matter-spectrum examples test how many particles and species are needed to reproduce an arbitrary discrete charge. Highly charged states can invalidate the single-field discharge argument, while a genuinely large species count can supply an independent reason for a low cutoff.

The authors use a black-hole thought experiment: deposit charge of order N into a macroscopic hole, demand its return during evaporation, and identify the radius at which Schwarzschild behavior must change with Λ⁻¹. Combining the energy needed for discharge with MBH∼RBH MP² gives a cutoff estimate.

Use the stabilized supergravity mass matrix and canonical eigenstates; expand gauge kinetic functions, matter metrics and Higgs bilinears to obtain decay couplings. Include leading RG effects from top Yukawa and strong gauge interactions and compute two-body widths. Standard-model fermion and three-body channels are neglected as comparatively suppressed.

Follow damped scalar oscillations, Friedmann evolution, sequential decay reheating and entropy dilution. Apply the LSP Boltzmann equation to distinguish annihilation down to a critical density from a small-yield regime retaining the decay branching dependence.
Decompose G_i=αK_i+N_i with K^iN_i=0, and complete squares as σ=−2s_i s^i+ω. Optimizing α simplifies the sign problem; with two moduli, s_i can be set to zero and a cubic discriminant controls ω.

Use Kähler-covariant stationarity and Hessian formulas, then project the Hermitian mass block along the Goldstino direction. Superpotential derivatives are adjusted to eliminate the holomorphic Hessian block and give orthogonal multiplets large positive masses.

Orientifold-truncate N=2 prepotential data to obtain N=1 K and W, solve the dilaton/Kähler F-terms, and analyze the scalar potential. The appendix matches these equations to the mirror IIB ISD condition G₃=−i⋆G₃, including the corrected prepotential.

Use two-stage stabilization: integrate out T and S near vanishing F-terms, then expand the complex-structure potential through order ℳV′⁻³ with nonperturbative terms. A mirror Swiss-cheese form reduces it to the imported LARGE-volume potential structure.

Extract flux-dependent FI coefficients from derivatives of the gauged Kähler potential; combine them with the DBI auxiliary-field contribution and brane/orientifold tensions, impose R-R tadpole cancellation, and eliminate the real auxiliary field.

Formulate N=2 vector and single-tensor multiplets in N=1 superspace using two real superfields; construct interactions through a holomorphic prepotential and vector–tensor couplings generated by solutions of a Laplace equation, including Stückelberg gauging.

Apply the imported nonlinear-constraint construction to eliminate the chiral component X of the N=2 Maxwell multiplet. The surviving vector multiplet contains the second-supersymmetry Goldstino, and solving the constraint produces the supersymmetric Born–Infeld action.

Regularize localization by tracing over the complement of V, then subtract the entropy and modular-energy expectation of the vacuum reduced to the identical region. Define the modular Hamiltonian through ρ0V=exp(−K)/tr exp(−K).

For the scalar example, trace the Rindler-mode states explicitly and obtain an analytic entropy expression by representing log N as an integral and solving an auxiliary differential equation. Extract fixed-species and large-species asymptotics.

Use imported information-theoretic properties: relative-entropy positivity, joint convexity and monotonicity under restriction or completely positive trace-preserving evolution. In the GSL discussion, combine monotonicity with the quasistatic black-hole entropy–energy relation.

For a special Hermitian isotropic diffusion operator, use an eigenfunction expansion and imported localization results to discuss finite-time evolution. Separate the extended zero mode controlling finite-island equilibrium from excited modes potentially affecting earlier evolution.

Expand nearest-neighbor master equations to second order in a continuum coordinate. Symmetric rate fluctuations become fluctuating diffusion coefficients, while antisymmetric fluctuations become a random-force term. Optional volume growth and AdS sinks enter through (3H−Γs)P.

Construct Martin–Siggia–Rose response-field functionals, average Gaussian disorder to obtain effective interactions, and use scaling and dynamical RG near N=2. The justification for replacing moduli-space averages by disorder averages invokes ergodicity in weak-disorder perturbation theory.

Use Ωh, or y=1/√Ωh, to parameterize late evolution, matching the integration constant through continuity at radiation–dark-energy equality. Expand the implicit solution in the matter-dominated and dark-energy-dominated limits.

Solve the Friedmann equation separately in the three phases and match quantities at their boundaries. Radiation-plus-matter evolution is treated exactly within its truncated energy content; the matter-plus-holographic-dark-energy phase uses previously published implicit solutions.

Extract leading small-cs cubic interactions, calculate the purely adiabatic and mixed adiabatic–entropy three-point functions, symmetrize the mixed contribution, and use linear entropy-to-curvature transfer to obtain the retained observable curvature bispectrum.

Use field-space covariant derivatives and an effective metric G̃IJ=⊥IJ+cs^-2 eσI eσJ. Canonically normalize the adiabatic and entropy variables separately and solve their approximately decoupled mode equations with a Minkowski-like short-wavelength vacuum.

Expand the DBI determinant using antisymmetrized field indices, retaining terms higher order in spacetime gradients. Introduce X̃=(1−D)/(2f), then expand the constrained scalar-plus-metric action to quadratic order in flat-gauge field perturbations QI.

Expand in λ while evaluating the Liouville sector exactly. For external operators with fixed X¹ and X⁰ charges, charge conservation selects only one perturbative order in the correlator used to diagnose nonholomorphicity.

Refine Liouville higher equations of motion using the exact three-point structure constant, logarithmic vertex V′₀, and a distributional limit with α→0 and α₁−α₂→0. Applying the Laplacian extracts contact terms omitted by the contact-free operator equation.

Use the stress-tensor trace and virial-current improvement criterion: scale invariance requires T^μ_μ=−∂μJ^μ; in two dimensions a trace expressible as a Laplacian permits improvement to a traceless tensor.

Expand the supergravity potential through the stated order 1/V³, separating dominant volume/heavy-modulus terms from light-modulus corrections. Stabilize heavy axions at aiθi=π and impose approximate stationarity in the volume and heavy geometric directions.

Integrate background equations with fourth-order Runge–Kutta. Solve the coupled gauge-invariant perturbation equations twice for independent initial curvature and entropy vacuum modes, initialized deep inside the Hubble radius with cutoff ratio Cq≈100; combine the solutions into spectra and their cross-correlation.
Redefine light fields proportionally to τi^(3/4), then rotate to φ and χ. The subsequent analysis uses a diagonal field-space metric with components 2cos²α and 2sin²α, where cos(2α)=9(φ²−χ²)/8.

Follow decay chains with ISAJET/ISASUSY and simulate hadronization with PYTHIA. Vary standard and nonstandard reaction rates by Monte Carlo; combine theoretical and observational errors in quadrature in the χ² analysis.

Add photo-dissociation, hadro-dissociation, p↔n conversion and charged-relic catalysis to a standard BBN code. Evolve photon, electron and hadron distributions with Boltzmann equations and obtain nuclear reaction rates from spectra and cross sections.

Numerically integrate coupled gravitino-production, inflaton-energy and radiation-energy equations. For staus, solve coupled Boltzmann equations for helium–stau and hydrogen–stau bound states rather than imposing Saha equilibrium.

Use special Kähler geometry, a cubic prepotential and a Calabi–Visentini symplectic frame; gauge axionic translations with bulk fluxes and integrate out fields made massive in representative N=1 vacua.

Dimensionally reduce D3/D7 DBI actions and solve the compact-space Poisson equation for D3 backreaction. Compare the resulting Green-function gauge thresholds with open-string one-loop calculations and construct the corrected gaugino-condensate superpotential.

Integrate out the K3 modulus through DsW=0, expand the inflaton potential and kinetic term, and analyze slow-roll evolution analytically and numerically. Phenomenological estimates normally use 60 e-folds; Appendix F examines quartic corrections and canonical normalization.

Evaluate the real-part integrals numerically without expanding thermal distributions. Define singular integrals by principal values, extrapolate the excluded interval ε to zero, then fit small-coupling results to extract the coefficient linear in coupling in Σ(mf)/mf.

Use HTL-dressed one-loop diagrams, including the four-point-vertex contribution, with loop momentum integrated over its full range. The paper states these contain all NLO contributions plus higher-order terms. Real-time Keldysh sums, KMS conditions, HTL Ward identities and stationary-fermion vertex expressions reduce the integrands to self-energy functions.
Expand the retarded pole equation q0−Σ(q0)=0 about the LO solution mf. Since ImΣHTL=0 and ReΣHTL=e²T²/(8q0), the linearized corrections are M(1)=ReΣNLO(mf)/2 and γ(1)=−ImΣNLO(mf)/2.

Expand the F-term potential in the large-volume limit and classify inverse Kähler-metric scalings. Homogeneity and intersection data connect K^{jj}∼𝒱√τj to isolated local blow-ups and K^{11}∼τ₁² to K3-fibre behaviour.

Estimate loop corrections from KK and winding exchange, use extended no-scale cancellation, and compare the surviving scalar-potential scaling with the supergravity Coleman–Weinberg potential using a compactification-scale cutoff.

Minimise axion phases and test Hessian positivity, including a Cholesky decomposition for two small cycles. Compare competing volume powers and exponentials to decide whether small moduli can satisfy ajτj≫1 and leave an AdS volume minimum.

Represent D7s by a holomorphic tachyon T:E′→E, E′=σ*E*, with support detT=0. The worldvolume bundle is obtained from the quotient (E/TE′)|Σ tensored with KΣ^(−1/2). Cofactor equations locate flux-dual curves; polynomial counting and quotienting by bundle automorphisms yield moduli and matter.

Introduce an auxiliary parameter surface Σ by blowing up the double-intersection curve and taking the proper transform: ξt=η, t²=χ, ξ²=h. Its projection separates the two branches away from pinch points. This parametrizes the worldvolume rather than physically resolving the ambient space.

Use adjunction and Chern classes for Euler characteristics, topological and holomorphic Lefschetz formulas for orientifold eigenspaces, and Poincaré residues to identify allowed infinitesimal D7 deformations with odd holomorphic two-forms on Σ.
For Δ=−∇²+E1+E2, cutoff types I, II and III use −∇², −∇²+E1 and full Δ respectively; E2 contains couplings. Type III is spectrally adjusted. Most explicit calculations use an optimized profile.

The functional equation ∂tΓk = ½ Tr[(Γk^(2)+Rk)^−1∂tRk] supplies the beta functional. Finite operator projections yield coupling beta functions; coupling-dependent regulators can require solving algebraic equations for them.
Heat-kernel expansions and Mellin Q-functionals evaluate operator traces. Polynomial f(R) beta functions are extracted by curvature derivatives at R=0 using algebraic manipulation software.

Run GUT-scale boundaries using modified SPheno2.2.3 and iterative loop-corrected REWSB, including the predicted B condition. Compute relic density with micrOMEGAs and impose historical mass/rare-decay bounds. Muon g−2 compatibility is displayed but not imposed.
Infer matter-metric scaling Kα ∝ t^(1−ξα)/tb from Kähler-modulus-independent holomorphic Yukawas and overlap integrals of normalized internal wavefunctions; compare with explicit toroidal results.

Apply a Rayleigh bound to the minimum eigenvalue of the normalized covariant Hessian. Averaging projections along two orthogonal real sGoldstino directions eliminates the holomorphic Hessian block and isolates the sectional-curvature obstruction.

Minimize holomorphic sectional curvature over unit Goldstino vectors to obtain a test of K alone. Local superpotential derivatives are then used to tune the gradient and Hessian entries not fixed by the Goldstino projection.

For the conifold, rewrite the metric integral as a boundary term. Replace the full throat by a hard-wall approximation, solve radial compensator equations near the infrared boundary, and fix their normalization by matching to the KS fluctuation norm.

Use Yang–Mills Gauss-law reduction as a guide, then ADM Hamiltonian momentum constraints to project out diffeomorphisms. The displayed 4d gravitational metric is G_IJ=¼∫√g e^(2A) δI g_ij δJ π^ij, with δπ_ij=δg_ij+½g_ij tr_g(δg), subject to warped transversality.

Use locally inertial coordinates and quadratic Hessian symmetries near extrema to constrain Euclidean paths. For the HM-connected class, the stated single-pass CDL criterion is |λᵢ|>4ε²VN(HM) along a negative-eigenvalue symmetry direction; other weak-gravity classes are not excluded.

Choose plausible paths through minima and an intervening HM saddle, canonically normalize along each path, solve the resulting one-dimensional Euclidean gravity problem, and evaluate its background-subtracted WKB action. These are approximate constrained-path constructions.

Compute periods using Maple Meijer G-functions on a grid with ΔzR=ΔzI=0.04, minimize τ at each z, and interpolate the potential. Classical flat-FRW trajectories are integrated using an adapted Supercosmology program.

Worldsheet and boundary CFT: use BRST invariance and conformal dimensions to construct closed-string massless-vector vertices from currents. Open-string boundary vertices have different dimension requirements; Chan–Paton labels carry no conformal dimension.

Analyse two U(1) fields with kinetic matrix Z and mass matrix M²: canonically normalise with Z^{-1/2}, then rotate to diagonalise Z^{-1/2}M²Z^{-1/2}. Examine massive, massless and zero-kinetic-mixing limits.

Treat the finite-volume local metric as a perturbation of its noncompact limit. Relate isometries to rotations among Dirac zero-mode solutions, and identify symmetry-breaking metric deformations with charged Kaluza–Klein modes.

Analyze exotic mass matrices generated by singlet VEVs using superpotentials known through sixth order in MSSM singlets; solve Model 1A F-flatness conditions with superpotential coefficients set to one.

Numerically solve effective one-loop RGEs with exotic thresholds and logarithmic plus universal power-law KK contributions. Match coupling differences and an absolute coupling at Mex to a 4D SUSY GUT reference incorporating approximate two-loop/SUSY-threshold effects and a 3% strong-coupling threshold.

Delete Dynkin nodes, project roots onto finite-subalgebra weight spaces and orthogonal directions, and impose integer root coefficients, index constraints, connected support and allowed squared lengths.

For a rank-p spacetime charge, the authors obtain mD=p+1+kD with k≥0; k counts spacetime volume-form blocks. Matching internal highest weights, including sums of fundamental weights, identifies candidate multiplets.

A Cartan-truncated group element is interpreted through a diagonal vielbein. Basis changes from Cartan generators to diagonal generators and then to the ei basis turn the proposed charge matrix element into an exponential mass expression.
The author assembles conceptual critiques involving high-energy fluctuation suppression, complementarity, Planck-scale observer distinguishability, de Sitter observables and Boltzmann brains.

An imported EFT power-counting argument questions control of a generic potential expansion over chaotic-inflation trajectories with Δφ>Mp. A field shift is said not to restore control along the whole trajectory.

Compare stochastic inflaton displacement with classical drift, then test the resulting eternal-inflation condition against effective-field-theory cutoffs, energy bounds or perturbativity requirements.

Bundle-valued Dolbeault cohomology, vanishing theorems and index formulas count zero modes. On the relevant del Pezzo surfaces, simultaneous vanishing for L and L inverse is related to root classes with K_S·c1(L)=0 and c1(L)^2=-2.
A Hodge/Laplacian identity in a unitary frame estimates singlet profiles; their L2 norms determine physical couplings. Repelled profiles are normalized using a cutoff at the transverse scale R_perp.

Yukawas are estimated from triple intersections and canonically normalized wave-function overlaps. Hypercharge-induced Aharonov-Bohm distortions provide a qualitative explanation of increasingly violated GUT mass relations for lighter generations.
For 1+1-dimensional CFTs, map the plane to the thermal cylinder, transform density correlators, integrate for susceptibility, and analytically continue the Fourier-space result to real frequency.

An ADM expansion in spatially flat gauge eliminates lapse and shift through constraints and constructs quadratic and cubic actions for field perturbations.

Determinant identities and antisymmetrized field-index expansions express the DBI action through X^IJ. In four spacetime dimensions the determinant expansion terminates at order f^4 even for more than four fields.

Bayesian MCMC compares flat and radiative electroweak symmetry breaking (REWSB) priors. The REWSB Jacobian weights lower tan β and μ. Ten independent chains of 100,000 steps discard 4,000 burn-in steps; the reported final Gelman–Rubin statistic is 1.002.

FRW evolution and the continuity equation give density scaling with the scale factor. An ultralocal Kasner analysis compares the growth of shear with that of ekpyrotic matter during contraction.

Nonperturbative consistency is assessed using the Hamiltonian conjugate to x+, a nonstandard x+ Wick rotation, and background-dependent causal cones.

Soft terms follow from spurion continuation of gauge kinetic functions and matter metrics into superspace, with compensator-dependent renormalization, messenger matching, and RG evolution above and below the threshold.

Count cutoff KK states in either momentum or localized-coordinate bases. Localized contributions are integrated over sites intersecting the horizon; plane-wave contributions are weighted by their intersection probability with the small higher-dimensional black hole.

Apply the imported Lyth end-of-inflation mechanism and δN formalism to radial and light angular fields. Linear derivatives give the separate power contributions; higher derivatives are used to estimate fNL.

Expand the action to quadratic order about a maximally symmetric vacuum and analyze tensor, vector and scalar perturbations. Use the generalized Birkhoff theorem to distinguish freely propagating tensor modes from the constrained modes sourced by spherical solutions.

Evaluate bubble and wall energies with Hamiltonian boundary expressions. Compute the semiclassical nucleation exponent from the Euclidean bounce action relative to its background, and separately construct regular five-dimensional black-hole pair-production instantons.

Compare the inflationary H²h⁻² contribution in the warp-factor Einstein equation with the warp factor required by the DBI speed limit. Solve the constant-negative-bulk-potential example and examine a power-law generalization h=(r/R)^α.

Expand the probe-brane trajectory around the near-horizon speed of light, using the DBI equation of motion, RR potential and inflaton potential. Infer Lorentz-factor growth and apply the imported probe-consistency requirement that throat charge greatly exceed γ.

Use eight conserved SU(2,1) Noether charges. Under SO(4) invariance their radial components are constants. Algebraically eliminate axions in favor of the dilaton, obtain a first-order dilaton equation, a quadratic charge relation fixing c, and a cubic charge constraint.

Test supersymmetry through a zero eigenvalue of the radial quaternionic vielbein in the hyperino variation. Check the gravitino equation's integrability after imposing extremality, and calculate instanton actions from the charge-projection surface term.

For one field, an alternative local argument writes log V=2 Re(log ∂zW) where ∂zW is nonzero. The minimum principle for real parts of holomorphic functions excludes a nonconstant local minimum. The paper explicitly says this shortcut does not readily generalize to multiple fields.

The mixed-direction steps require the stated hierarchy z1^K≫zi≫z1^(K+1).

Evaluate the supergravity F-term potential using α′ and nonperturbative corrections, minimize the blow-up axion and stabilize 𝒱,τ3, then lift the remaining direction with a conjectured loop-correction form. Logarithmic canonical normalization converts inverse-cycle powers into exponentials.

Uses orientifold cohomology, superpotential holomorphy, large-volume suppression and instanton zero-mode arguments to assess which axion-dependent corrections can arise.

String statistical mechanics supplies a density-of-states expansion near the Hagedorn temperature. Metric derivatives of the partition function generate stress-tensor correlators; temperature derivatives yield density variance through T²CV/R⁶.

Dilaton-gravity background equations are supplemented by effective Boltzmann equations transferring energy from oppositely wound strings into unwound loops. Fundamental-string interaction coefficients depend on the dilaton.

The authors report second-order convergence under successive factor-two refinements, errors approximately at or below 0.1%, and disagreement between integration schemes approximately at or below 1%. Rapid variation near the outer horizon produces error spikes.

A slow-background derivative expansion localizes the response and gives Υ=(i/2)∂ωΣρ(0,ω)|ω=0. Spectral-function calculations determine coefficients; a quasiparticle Boltzmann treatment separately connects particle-production sources to the radiation energy equation.

A Hubbard–Stratonovich transformation of the effective action, truncated at quadratic order in φΔ, introduces Gaussian stochastic noise. The retarded self-energy supplies causal response, and the noise covariance is ΣF.

Shift the seed's asymptotic radius above one, rotate its charge into a ten-dimensional gauge U(1), and rescale the final internal modulus. This isolates a finite Wilson-line-zero locus outside the repulson without relying on geometric self-duality there.

Find the charged-state massless locus, form the corresponding enhançon shell, and replace the singular interior with a regular interior. The operation depends on the quantum charged spectrum and cannot be applied using the classical radius profile alone.

Use a compact Euclidean CDL ansatz and regularity conditions at both poles, an inverted-potential mechanical analogy, and thin-wall integration of the χ equation; compare the induced kinetic energy with the stabilizing barrier.

Define n=l/resolution, N=n^d, δN=n^4−N and the dimension deficit ε=4−d. The author expands the logarithmic box-counting expression to ε≈δN/(n^4 ln n), identifying missing occupied cells with a volume deficit.

Weyl limit-point criteria establish essential self-adjointness. Interval decomposition, asymptotic-potential spectral theorems and integrability estimates determine essential and absolutely continuous spectra; Levinson asymptotics address a possible ultracold-I zero mode.

Construct a finite null modulus wave with covariant ten-dimensional equations; study strong-warping wavefunctions through local AdS estimates and numerical compensator solutions in a Klebanov-Strassler throat.

Sum multiparticle transition probabilities for vacuum creation, induced creation and annihilation, then express their net contribution as a thermal trace of the outgoing-minus-incoming total occupation. Evaluate the trace using Bose or Fermi occupation sums.

Represent incoming-to-outgoing Bogoliubov transformations by modewise unitary evolution/squeezing operators, with parameters determined by μ and ν. The zero-temperature baseline is Nn(0) = |νn|² for both statistics.

Collider estimates use MadGraph QED backgrounds, Monte Carlo on-shell U production and decay, geometric cuts, and Gaussian detector smearing. Visible branching fractions are inferred from measured electromagnetic R values; the pion channel uses an empirical pion form factor.

Meson estimates compare narrow U peaks with virtual-photon dilepton backgrounds. The detailed φ→ηU analysis uses an effective VPγ interaction, a form factor normalized at zero virtuality, and explicit phase-space factors.

Fixed-target projections combine analytic luminosity and background-rate estimates with ionization-loss estimates, pile-up constraints and a maximum readout rate. These are order-of-magnitude design calculations rather than a complete detector simulation.

Studies nodal degenerations and curve factorization while keeping mass residues finite; matches the resulting components to decoupled gauge theories and checks Coulomb-branch dimensions against spaces of meromorphic differentials.
Uses Newton polygons to relate pole orders to local sheet branching, and flavor-current anomalies/conformal beta-function requirements to constrain possible gauging and emergent gauge groups.
Imports brane-derived Seiberg-Witten curves for linear unitary quivers, then changes coordinates and shifts the fiber variable to expose puncture symmetries and the canonical differential.

Counts derivatives and internal lines in 1PI diagrams, improves ghost counting using the asserted graviton transversality, and combines the divergence bound with a linearized Slavnov-Taylor renormalization equation to classify local counterterms.
Expands quadratic metric fluctuations in spin-2, spin-1, scalar, longitudinal, and mixed projection operators, then inverts the quadratic operator to analyze propagator components and poles.

BRST gauge fixing uses de Donder gauge for diffeomorphisms and a Landau-like condition for the Stückelberg vector. Sources for BRST variations are introduced to derive Slavnov-Taylor identities for the effective action.

Estimates the formation fraction with Gaussian fluctuations: β_i≈σ_H exp[−δ_min²/(2σ_H²)]/(√(2π)δ_min), using δ_min≈0.3 and σ_H(T_0)=9.5×10^−5. A chosen small-scale spectral index controls the horizon-crossing variance.

Illustrates q/m∼1 evolution with discrete emissions and approximate energy loss ΔM=m+Qq/R_h. For the stated initial M=2000 M_Pl and Q=1000q, the trajectories reach extremality above an initial Q/M of approximately 0.725.

Computes present remnant density from initial PBH abundance, dilution, and the ratio M_rel/M_i, imposing Ω_rel,0<1. Scans initial PBH mass and particle mass using formation temperature and a prescribed remnant mass.
Specifies GUT-scale mirage-mediated soft terms and anomalous dimensions, then uses RG evolution to illustrate gaugino and scalar spectra and obtain alternative LSP assignments.
Uses the damped scalar equation in FRW, coupled modulus/radiation/dark-matter Boltzmann equations, a sudden-decay reheating approximation, and an annihilation-attractor estimate for the final yield.

Open-string disk correlators reduce to Euler Beta functions; their pole expansions organize Regge exchange. Collider estimates broaden resonances with Breit–Wigner widths and combine partonic processes with parton distributions.

Flux analysis uses Killing-spinor equations, SU(3) torsion classes, pure-spinor generalized geometry and effective-supergravity Kähler/superpotential extrema. Intersecting or smeared brane domain walls provide a complementary description of flux sources and AdS near-horizon regions.

Landscape searches solve supersymmetry, RR-tadpole and K-theory restrictions on integer brane-wrapping data. The review discusses Diophantine enumeration, saddle-point counting estimates and statistical correlations within specified orientifold ensembles.
Split the F-term potential into V0 and positive bundle-dependent square terms δV0. Uplift requires kα^I∂IW+∂αW≠0 for at least one bundle modulus α, and therefore entails supersymmetry breaking.

Use a logarithmic-Kähler toy model, expansions in inverse nonperturbative actions, extremum and Hessian conditions, and numerical searches. The authors explicitly describe part of the heterotic construction as numerical trial and error.

Compare regularized Euclidean black-hole and Horowitz–Myers soliton actions, matching boundary periodicities. The soliton is obtained through double analytic continuation, and its parameters need not coincide with the black-hole parameters.

Write the horizon equation as a cubic in x=r², select its larger positive root, and evaluate the large-radius brane action. The instability threshold follows when its positive horizon contribution ceases to offset the negative mass contribution.

Diagonalize permutation-symmetric matrices with common diagonal and off-diagonal entries. The neutron problem reduces to our neutron plus one democratic hidden combination; a magnetic potential supplies a two-state resonance.

Use inclusive production rates and loop sums over species to constrain couplings by unitarity and perturbativity. Apply dimensional estimates to graviton exchange and effective operators generated by unspecified gravitational states near the cutoff.

Combine tadpole and SUSY constraints to bound winding numbers. The First Winding Number Bound constrains otherwise unbounded windings; the Two Column SUSY Bound requires at least one of two positive-column sums to be ≤T. Authors state polynomial-in-T enumeration algorithms.

For fixed G, loop over A-brane configurations, add bounded B/C stacks, test common linear SUSY constraints, then remove extra branes and canonicalize to eliminate duplicate realizations. The authors claim polynomial-time enumeration for fixed G.

Expand the metric and B-field in invariant tensors/forms, integrate internal Hodge contractions, and dualize the four-dimensional two-form to an axion. Nonclosed invariant two-forms generate bi dωi terms. Scalar redefinitions make radius limits transparent while preserving kinetic normalization.

Determine W from the heterotic formula W=(1/4)∫Ω∧(Ĥ+i dJ), and K from the dilaton contribution plus minus the logarithm of the internal volume. Compare the resulting N=1 potential and kinetic terms with the reduced action.

Coset Space Dimensional Reduction imposes L_X Â=D W_X and associated consistency conditions. Surviving gauge fields lie in H=C_G(R_G); scalar and spinor multiplets follow by matching isotropy representations. Gauge reduction imposes Dφi=Fij=Fai=0.

Scalar equations are treated as harmonic-map equations. Totally geodesic flat targets reduce them to linear harmonic equations; symmetric targets admit a Lie-triple-system description. A Bogomol'nyi square completion supplies the instanton action bound.

Conical Lagrangian immersions and homogeneous prepotentials encode the geometry. Quotienting is implemented by gauge fixing a gauged sigma model; its composite connection is dual to the pulled-back universal bundle's Chern connection.

Classify candidate relevant Lorentz scalars by global representations and inherited dimensions, including single- and double-trace operators. For the compact model, test the surviving discrete group's action on the low-dimensional KW spectrum.

Combine a spacetime orbifold action with a block-diagonal embedding in the parent gauge group. Determine daughter quivers and the light supergravity spectrum by retaining invariant fields and KK modes.

Bound/free populations are described by coupled Boltzmann equations, using the Milne relation and Coulomb bound-state wavefunctions. Late self-interaction bounds use Rutherford energy transfer with Debye screening and an angular integral for Bullet Cluster particle loss.

CalcHEP scattering amplitudes and a low-temperature collision expansion supply the momentum-transfer rate in a phase-space Boltzmann equation. Kinetic decoupling is defined by equality of momentum-transfer and Hubble rates, including hidden-photon Compton and hidden-neutrino scattering.

Fourier perturbations in conformal Newtonian gauge track hidden-radiation multipoles through lmax=10, followed by free-streaming evolution. The cutoff kcut is the first transfer-function drop to 1/e; the minimum halo mass is estimated from the mean matter mass within radius π/kcut.

Standard Hamilton–Jacobi canonical transformations generate first-order equations through pi=∂iW and q̇i=Gij∂jW. Constant new momenta encode integration constants; the original energy constraint supplies the Hamilton–Jacobi equation.

The local characteristic function is expressed as an on-shell trajectory integral: W=W0+∫(c²+L)dτ=W0+2∫(c²+𝒱)dτ. An equivalent eikonal construction uses characteristics and their configuration-space proper distance.

Applications include Reissner–Nordström, N=2 BPS flows with full characteristic function 2eU|Z|, and restricted-charge non-BPS solutions in the one-modulus cubic model. The examples illustrate the formalism rather than supply a general explicit all-charge solution.

Separates the massive scalar equation on Kerr into angular and radial problems, recasts the latter as a frequency-dependent Schrödinger problem, and illustrates growth with a barrier toy model. Simplified occupation-number equations model gravitational-wave transitions and accretion.

Reviews linear scalar perturbations in Newtonian gauge with anisotropic stress neglected. An oscillation-averaged, nonrelativistic treatment gives momentum-dependent sound speed c_s² = k²/(4m²a²), followed by estimates of altered matter growth and misalignment abundance.

Uses cohomological KK reduction and geometric estimates of decay constants and instanton actions. Nonperturbative potentials are parametrized by exponentially suppressed scales, allowing masses to vary much more strongly than decay constants.

Generalized dimensional reduction of NSNS and RR vector field strengths is matched to standard N = 4 non-Abelian curvatures. This identifies flux-dependent generalized structure constants and thereby fixes the two-derivative gauged action.

Supersymmetry is analyzed through fermion-shift matrices, the scalar-potential Ward identity, and explicit coset representatives. The preserved direction qᴵ = δᴵ₄ reconstructs N = 1 F-terms and is asserted to be the unique surviving supersymmetry.

Scalar covariant derivatives select electric vector combinations. Orthogonality to magnetic combinations follows using flux constraints; partial solution of RR Bianchi identities removes unwanted tensors while retaining the necessary scalar and vector components.

Use group trace identities to remove irreducible tr F^4 anomalies, then solve Green–Schwarz factorization of the remaining polynomial. For the worked model the irreducible constraints are M−BN=8 and 2N−A(N−8)−BM=0.

Compare the resulting algebraic constraints with D9/D5 tadpole cancellation and index-theorem matter multiplicities on K3. Independently examine supersymmetry-related gauge kinetic coefficients and use gravitational-anomaly scaling to constrain large-rank SU(N) matter.

Compute the Euclidean determinant through the spectral zeta function of μ²−D², with W_E=½ζ′(0), then continue eE→ieE. KK factorization, heat-kernel degeneracies and Hurwitz-zeta identities are used; Nariai additionally uses Abel–Plana transformations.

Use diagonal fermionic Bogoliubov transformations and Thermofield Dynamics to compute outgoing occupations in an incoming KMS state. Deviations from the incoming thermal occupation define the net pair-production contribution.

Separate the Dirac equation into angular modes and a two-dimensional equation, applying unitary Pauli-matrix rotations. Exact solutions use parabolic-cylinder functions for ultracold II, Kummer functions for ultracold I, and Gauss hypergeometric functions for Nariai.

Determine relative signed twisted-modulus couplings by factoring the vacuum tadpole out of the B² annulus UV amplitude. B⁴ exchange alone determines squared couplings and loses these signs. Compare the result with supergravity after linear-to-chiral multiplet dualization.

Use a background spacetime magnetic field F23=BQ and expand the one-loop vacuum energy. Its B² coefficient supplies the gauge threshold, with annulus and Möbius contributions; open–closed duality relates open-channel UV behavior to closed-channel tadpoles.

Construct spectra with orbifold and orientifold Chan–Paton projections. Extract fully twisted RR tadpoles from annulus, Möbius and Klein-bottle amplitudes; impose their cancellation to obtain consistent brane multiplicities and non-abelian anomaly conditions.

Use Ω-deformed localization on R4. U(2) fixed instantons are labeled by pairs of Young diagrams, weighted by powers of the exponentiated UV coupling and vector/hypermultiplet factors. Split Z_full into classical, one-loop and instanton pieces.

Compute Virasoro blocks by sewing descendant matrix elements using inverse Gram matrices. Compare their series with instanton sums after removing proposed U(1) factors; rewrite DOZZ structure constants using Barnes double-Gamma identities to identify one-loop factors and integration measures.

Insert T(z) into a conformal block using Virasoro Ward identities. Define φ2(z)=−⟨T(z)∏O_i⟩/⟨∏O_i⟩ and compare periods of its square root with Seiberg–Witten mass and Coulomb periods in the semiclassical limit.

Locality and volume independence of physical Yukawas are used as scaling arguments for Zα∼V^(−2/3). Matching the corrected bulk Kähler potential motivates α′³ as the first expected bulk-dependent matter-metric correction; its coefficient is not calculated.

Four-dimensional supergravity formulas for F-terms, gaugino masses, scalar masses and other soft parameters are expanded beyond leading order in inverse volume. Leading cancellations require retaining corrections in 1/(aτs) and contributions from the uplifting sector.

Numerically integrate the covariant Kähler-field equations in spatially flat FRW, including Hubble friction, field-space connection terms and the Friedmann constraint. Displace τ2, locate conditional minima in other directions and subsequently test trajectories starting away from them.

Estimate the adiabatic spectrum along numerical trajectories using P(N)=V(N)/(150π²ε(N)), ε=K^(i j̄)∇_iV∇_j̄V/V² and n_s=1+d ln P/dN. Compare these estimates with the earlier canonically normalized single-field slow-roll approximation.
Expand g = ḡ + λh + λ²j + … and ψ = λψ(1) + λ²ψ(2) + …. Bosonic and fermionic equations decouple at linear order because their torsional coupling begins at second order.

Compute energy through the Abbott–Deser–Tekin construction from quadratic effective sources. Obtain supercharges by contracting the expanded gravitino equation with background Killing spinors, retaining terms through λ².

Construct harmonic primary modes using the SL(2,R) generators, Casimir equations and Lie derivatives on tensors/vector-spinors. Use transverse traceless metric perturbations and gamma-traceless gravitini.

Exterior calculus is used to describe Holst and Nieh–Yan actions and their torsion equations. In supergravity, Majorana Fierz identities establish the special on-shell identity tr(T∧T)=0 for gravitino-generated torsion.

For the field-valued coupling, a super-Weyl transformation is performed entirely in superspace. The holomorphic choice Z=Φ yields a full-superspace chiral-matter action from which the kinetic and Kähler potentials are read.

The chiral superspace Einstein action is complexified by 1/κ²→(1+iη)/κ². Chiral density integration and Wess–Zumino component expansion identify its additional terms as a supersymmetric Holst extension.

Count quartic bulk interactions modulo total derivatives and equations of motion using Bose-symmetric flat-space polynomial amplitudes, with s+t+u=4m². Match this lower bound to the CFT upper bound at bounded exchanged spin.

Expand the four-point function into conformal blocks and linearize crossing in 1/N². Separate logarithmic terms, project with hypergeometric contour integrals J(p,q), and use nondegenerate matrices to bound the number of independent anomalous dimensions.

Calculate contact Witten diagrams using embedding-space propagators and D-functions. Use the Lorentzian Regge limit and harmonic analysis on hyperbolic space for maximal-spin data, and large-dimension saddle approximations for the scattering singularity.

Uses low-energy loop scaling and the Coleman–Weinberg potential to motivate corrections and cancellations; expresses the one-loop scalar potential through the tree-level Kähler metric and conjectured Kähler-potential correction.

Derives moduli–matter couplings by expanding supergravity functions and canonically normalizing fields; applies thermalization analysis and a high-temperature expansion to the finite-temperature potential.

Classifies large-volume scaling using the inverse Kähler metric and homogeneity; minimizes axion potentials and tests Hessian positivity, including a Cholesky decomposition for the two-axion analysis.
Derives universal scalings VR=URρ^-1τ^-2, VH=UHρ^-3τ^-2 and Vq=Uqρ^(3−q)τ^-4. For V=aτ^-2−bτ^-3+cτ^-4, uses stationary 4ac/b²≈1 as a diagnostic for small positive vacuum energy.
Chooses a flux ansatz satisfying ten-dimensional form equations first, then matches independent tensors in the internal Einstein equation and imposes its trace and the dilaton equation.
Solves for positive torsion norms as functions of flux ratios, examines the ρ–τ mass matrix, and tests torsion conditions using explicit coset and Iwasawa structure forms.

Evaluate next-order slow-roll expressions, but numerically solve the full Mukhanov–Sasaki equation when treating slow-roll parameters as constant is inaccurate. Extract observables from the resulting scalar spectrum at a chosen pivot.
Apply EFT power counting and a small-trilinear-coupling requirement. Combine the approximation α≈−2ξ² with r=16ε to relate running, tensor strength and Λ.

Use five inputs: three CMB-point slow-roll parameters, NCMB and φEND. Impose ε(φEND)=1 to determine a4 and the e-fold integral to determine a5. An expansion near the minimum of ε explains how a shallow region generates many e-folds.

Use constrained chiral superfields while retaining auxiliary fields: XNL² = 0 describes the Goldstino; XNL QNL = 0 removes a matter scalar; a chirality constraint removes the fermion of HNL; XNL(ANL − AbarNL) = 0 retains one real scalar.

Explicit examples integrate out massive scalars through zero-momentum equations of motion. Integration by parts, constrained field redefinitions and auxiliary equations organize the effective action and eliminate redundant operators.
Follow the chiral operator X in the Ferrara–Zumino equation Dbar J = D X along the RG flow, using its supercurrent and stress-tensor components to identify the infrared Goldstino operator.

Import horizon-crossing field two- and three-point functions, selecting a short-wavelength Minkowski-like vacuum. Insert these into the δN bispectrum and trispectrum expansions, separating intrinsic quantum, classical local and mixed contributions; examine selected momentum-space limits.
Use the separate-universe δN expansion ζ = NA QA + NAB QA QB/2 + NABC QA QB QC/6 + … . The local expansion integrates H/φ̇ from φ* to an angular-dependent end surface φe = [φc² − (βΞ*/cs*)²]¹ᐟ².

Fermi momenta are located numerically as normalizable zero-frequency Dirac bound states. Feynman–Hellmann-type variations express velocities and residues through bound-state integrals; WKB provides additional asymptotic information.

Matched asymptotic expansion separates an inner AdS2 problem from an outer radial problem. Infalling inner solutions supply the nonanalytic frequency dependence; outer solutions supply coefficients expanded perturbatively in frequency.

Dimensional reduction and N=1 Kähler geometry relate axion kinetics to compactification data. Moduli are integrated out perturbatively in the instanton factor; simplified geometries estimate backreaction, and string-derived higher-derivative terms are assessed using S-duality.

Modified CAMB and WMAP5 likelihood codes evaluate an oscillatory-spectrum parameter grid. Baryon density, scalar amplitude and phase are marginalized; several other cosmological parameters are fixed. Restricted CosmoMC runs provide an author-reported cross-check.

Perturbative background evolution and a Green-function solution of the Mukhanov–Sasaki equation, with a Weber–Schafheitlin integral for the modulation amplitude. Stationary phase and time-dependent particle-production estimates supply complementary interpretations.

KK spectral decomposition describes the effective brane graviton. Power counting of the scalar-helicity trilinear interaction determines nonlinear radii; BPS deficit-angle counting and D3 geometric scale relations provide additional examples.

Black-hole quasi-classicality and information-pixel arguments: resolving N labels requires a detector containing all N species, with minimum energy N/L, whose gravitational radius must not exceed its size.
BRST gauge fixing is implemented in Feynman gauge. A fictitious mass regulates gravitational infrared divergences by replacing 1/k⁴ with 1/(k²+z²)², followed by cancellation checks and z→0.

Dimensional regularization and Laurent counterterms retain conformal-mode dependence away from four dimensions. Products of pole residues with powers of D−4 induce finite Wess–Zumino vertices; commuting Weyl variations constrain admissible counterterms.

Composite-operator counterterms determine anomalous dimensions. A 't Hooft–Weinberg RG equation identifies its scale parameter with a constant conformal-mode shift; a one-loop log determinant and resummation produce the effective cosmological potential.

Derive Poisson brackets through Hamiltonian cut-and-glue flows. Encode coordinate changes by flips and pops, adding annular limit triangulations and juggles to accommodate infinitely twisted limits associated with vectormultiplets.

Choose phase-dependent WKB triangulations from trajectories satisfying λ(∂t)∈e^{iϑ}ℝ×. WKB estimates control parallel transport and decay of flat sections near punctures; finite trajectories identify exceptional phases at which triangulations jump.

Use the flat family 𝒜=Rϕ/ζ+A+Rζϕ̄ and decorated triangulations. For counterclockwise quadrilateral vertices with diagonal 1–3, define X_E=−(s₁∧s₂)(s₃∧s₄)/[(s₂∧s₃)(s₄∧s₁)]. The flat sections select monodromy eigenlines; rescalings cancel, giving coordinates on a Zariski open patch.

Spherical harmonics and transfer-function integrals connect primordial spectra to CMB angular correlations. Leading non-Gaussian effects require cubic interactions; their detailed derivation is largely replaced by a review of results.

Background evolution uses Friedmann and scalar equations, followed by a slow-roll approximation relating Hubble evolution to potential derivatives and expressing the remaining expansion as a field-space integral.

The scalar calculation expands the action to quadratic order, introduces v=zR with z²=a²φ̇²/H², and solves v_k''+(k²−z''/z)v_k=0. Canonical normalization and a subhorizon Minkowski boundary condition select the Bunch-Davies modes.

Combine slow evaporation and metastability conditions with the black-body emission law and wavelength bound. The authors obtain M R_S>N(β) and an additional inequality containing d ln R_S/d ln M, then argue that the latter supplies no independent restriction.

Use a two-observer collapse thought experiment and the equivalence principle to argue against a cutoff shorter than the minimum semiclassical black-hole scale: freely falling and distant observers should not disagree about a low-curvature collapse while remaining in causal contact.

Analyze the conserved-source one-particle exchange amplitude around flat spacetime using spin-2 and spin-0 contributions and positive ghost-free spectral weights. A Yukawa spectral integral is used to compare the gravitational field and black-hole mass with Einstein gravity.

Linear mode equations, Bunch-Davies boundary conditions and canonical Wronskians determine normalized perturbations. Linear response functions are then introduced through Π^(ζ)=Ωζ and Π^(γ)=Eγ, expressing power spectra through their late-time imaginary parts.

An imported Hamilton-Jacobi first-order formulation introduces a fake superpotential W(ϕ), with H=−W/2, when scalar evolution is piecewise monotonic. The paper relates this background formalism to the domain-wall/cosmology correspondence.

Domain-wall correlators are extracted using a radial Hamiltonian method and holographic renormalization, with Dirichlet data at infinity and regularity in the interior. The renormalized response coefficients determine the stress-tensor two-point function before analytic continuation.

Match IIB potential terms to IIA volume–dilaton scaling powers, including localized sources and axion dependence. The proposed subsequent search analytically eliminates S and T before numerical treatment of Z; details of the minimization procedure are deferred.

Solve Q²=0 and H̄₃Q=0 Jacobi constraints in canonical generator bases. Graded contractions and the Killing–Cartan matrix identify full algebras; in the κ₁=κ₁₂ branch, semisimplicity requires κ₁κ₂(κ₁ε₁²−κ₂ε₂²)≠0.

Use real fractional-linear GL(2,R) transformations U→Z to obtain canonical flux polynomials. Axion shifts and nonzero-parameter rescalings simplify the R-R sector and reduce the continuous effective-potential parametrization to two angles, θ_ε and θ_ξ.

Estimate stabilization through a dimensionally reduced Einstein-frame potential: positive internal curvature contributes negative potential energy, 7-branes offset it with the same inverse-length-squared scaling, and metric flux plus five-form flux complete the balance. F theory handles the strong 7-brane backreaction.

Use a two-dimensional (2,2) GLSM to describe the elliptic geometry. Vanishing sums of charges implement the Calabi-Yau condition; a Weierstrass superpotential encodes 7-branes through Δ=4f³+27g². Removing the radial field exposes an FI beta-function cancellation, giving ε∼w0/w.

Analyze singular branches using their GLSM central charge, including every massless field even without a flat direction. Quasihomogeneous superpotential weights determine contributions. Complexified FI parameters and holomorphic observables probe the marginal singularity at the cone tip.

In the dilute regime, redraw impact parameters uniformly in the transverse D−4 dimensions up to the mean separation on each estimated re-collision time. Temporarily freeze interactions to test whether winding-induced recollapse occurs before another collision can happen.

Transform the long-wound-string Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude into impact-parameter space in D−4 directions transverse to both strings' motion. Its imaginary part gives P(b)=Im A(s,b)/v. High-energy eikonal arguments motivate interpreting b semiclassically.

Integrate coupled dilaton-gravity and Boltzmann equations subject to the Hamiltonian constraint. Compare Hagedorn and radiation equilibrium prescriptions, switching according to E≤cd TH^(d+1)Vd. Scan an initial-condition grid with 1,000 randomized runs per point for d=3 through 9.

Use the supergravity vacuum potential and small vacuum energy to relate m3/2 to F/mp. Generic quadratic Kähler terms supply scalar mass contributions of order m3/2, motivating a relation between modulus masses and the supersymmetry-breaking spectrum.

Estimate gravitational decay through Γφ∼mφ³/mp² and instantaneous conversion of modulus energy. Compare injected dark-matter density with the critical annihilation density H/⟨σv⟩, then redshift the resulting nonthermal freeze-out abundance.

Use an infrared-regulated minisuperspace Wheeler–DeWitt expansion, select the expanding branch, and obtain an approximate Schrödinger equation for fluctuations at large scale factor. The boundary-area phase motivates a holographic replacement of bulk variables.

Review Euclidean thin-wall CDL correlators, analytically continue X→T+iπ/2 and θ→iR, and deform spectral contours into residue sums. The analysis restores lower-half-plane contributions omitted from the earlier late-time treatment.

Adapt the imported k-essence flow hierarchy and Hamilton–Jacobi formulation, using monotonic φ as a clock. Constant flow parameters reduce the hierarchy to algebraic relations and determine H(φ), cS(φ), and LX(φ).

Reconstruct actions through 2XLXX+LX−C(LX)^n=0, with n=1+2s/s̃. For perturbations, use u=zζ, z=a√(ρ+p)/(cSH), and y=cSk/(aH); constant flows give Hankel solutions, with Bunch–Davies initial conditions and canonical normalization.
Use QA-cohomology to represent supersymmetric vacua and the twisted chiral ring; use equivariant descent and the instanton partition function to compute the effective twisted superpotential.

Classical spectral curves and periods determine action variables and the prepotential. Formal ultraviolet source deformations tk generate observables, while derivatives of the deformed twisted superpotential generate quantum eigenvalues.

Represent the instanton contribution as a critical functional of density and auxiliary fields, yielding a TBA-like integral equation. Its derivation uses a one-dimensional instanton gas, Mayer expansion, clustering into dilogarithms, and surviving tree diagrams.

Decompose the gauge field into helicities, solve its mode equation with Coulomb wave functions and positive-frequency initial conditions, then approximate the amplified helicity to estimate ⟨E·B⟩ and gauge-field energy.

Compute sourced inflaton fluctuations using a retarded Green function and the two-point function of δ(E·B). Include feedback through the dependence of ⟨E·B⟩ on Φ̇, then convert to curvature perturbations using δN.

Describe compact-phase branes by graded matrix factorizations modulo a subcategory associated with the Cox ideal. Graded free resolutions and the map κ encode charges in Laurent polynomials; monodromy acts by a grading shift, represented by multiplication by s.

Treat rational K-theory as a module over the monodromy ring. Companion matrices and complex Jordan forms determine asymptotic periods; the symplectic period pairing then determines the Kähler potential, moduli metric and normalized central charges without explicitly solving Picard–Fuchs equations.

Transport branes between phases using tilting collections and mapping cones of trivial objects. Gröbner normal forms encode the transport, and Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch supplies the symplectic charge pairing needed for special Kähler geometry.

Estimate visible-sector decay rates by canonical normalization and diagonalization of mixed moduli, using gauge and fermion couplings and perturbative widths. Convert rates to reheat temperatures with Tr≈0.1√(ΓMP).

Introduce a canonical radial field φ and canonical axion fluctuation δψ=ebδθ. Solve oscillator-like fluctuation equations numerically and compute Floquet exponents to identify tachyonic growth and resonance bands.

Use nonlinear 512³ lattice simulations with noncanonical kinetic terms and self-consistent expansion. Start with vacuum modes in momentum space, then switch to configuration space at large occupation numbers, when gradient energy is about 10−4 of condensate energy.
Uses dimensional reduction of DBI and Chern–Simons actions to estimate gauge couplings and Stückelberg mass matrices, retaining dependence on cycle metrics, flux integrals and orientifold parity.

Estimates supersymmetry-breaking mixing through higher-dimensional superspace operators, messenger diagrams and toroidal four-gauge-boson amplitudes. Hidden Higgs hierarchies are studied by stabilizing and integrating out a Stückelberg-associated modulus.

Relates holomorphic and canonical kinetic mixing by extending the Kaplunovsky–Louis/rescaling treatment to multiple U(1)s. The paper asserts that its relation, including charged-matter metrics and the full Kähler potential, is exact in perturbation theory.

Construct Euclidean Klein–Gordon spectra and heat kernels, form spectral ζ-functions, and analytically continue eE→ieE to obtain the imaginary Lorentzian action. Hurwitz ζ-functions enter the ultracold calculations; heat-kernel matching fixes degeneracies such as eES/(2π).

Separate time, spherical harmonics and radial dependence. Radial equations are solved using parabolic-cylinder functions for ultracold II, confluent hypergeometric functions for ultracold I, and Gauss hypergeometric functions for Nariai. Asymptotic connection formulas determine scattering data.

Uses B-brane quantum curves and a Drinfeld–Sokolov connection for the probe derivation. For refinement, evaluates the Gaussian β-ensemble with a Selberg integral and compares its large-N free energy with a hypermultiplet contribution.

Rewrites eigenvalue integrals as free-boson Coulomb gases, interprets Vandermonde factors as screening correlations, and bosonizes free fermions. Matrix loop equations follow from infinitesimal changes of variables and become stress-tensor constraints.

Uses imported open/closed large-N duality: B-branes on resolved conifold spheres are replaced by deformed geometry, while the matrix-model resolvent and filling fractions determine the closed-string spectral curve.

The perturbation treatment combines field and metric fluctuations in conformal Newtonian gauge, separates adiabatic and isocurvature modes, and uses modified CAMB calculations to examine CMB and matter power spectra.

The no-go discussion analyzes gauge-invariant pressure, density and entropy perturbations, then scalar dispersion relations with c_s²=P_,X/ρ_,X. Negative sound-speed squared or a divergent dispersion relation supplies the stated obstruction to stable crossing.

Background models are converted into autonomous systems using normalized field variables and N=ln a; critical-point stability is assessed through eigenvalue real parts. The geometrical statefinder pair {r,s}, constructed from scale-factor derivatives, is used as a model diagnostic.

AdS/CFT motivates the construction: separate composite sectors have different compositeness scales; spontaneous conformal breaking identifies the waterfall with a dilaton-like mode, represented gravitationally by the radion. Relevant waterfall-sector operators correspond to AdS tachyonic scalars.

The authors integrate out bulk scalars using mixed position-momentum propagators at zero four-momentum, obtain the Wilson-loop potential from charged-scalar loops, and extremize the two-field potential to integrate out the heavy radion during inflation.

Computes the conformal transformation of Ricci curvature, imposes a vanishing-Ricci-scalar gauge, and studies infinitesimal Fourier modes of the scale function to identify a restricted class of massless stress-energy configurations.

Constructs a conformal inversion between the common flat regions of the incoming and outgoing shell pictures, choosing its sign to preserve timelike causal order. Null-shell matching is then used to discuss joining different conformal regions.
