Redefine fields and charge coefficients to compare reduced membrane equations with the sigma-model equations obtained by independently varying xμ and the auxiliary worldsheet metric h_ab. The comparison includes the electromagnetic modification of boundary conditions.

Use a covariant multipole expansion of stress-energy and spin, restricted to delta-function single-pole terms. Conservation laws, after eliminating antisymmetric stress-energy through the spin equation, determine worldsheet equations and boundary conditions without first choosing a matter action.

Functionals are finite combinations of even derivatives in a and b at z=z̄=1/2, with z=1/2+a+b and z̄=1/2+a−b. Setting Λ[1]=1 converts the stress-tensor bound into maximizing Λ[Fd,4,2] subject to nonnegativity on every allowed block vector.

The resulting optimization is linear programming. The described numerical procedure discretizes Δ and truncates large Δ and spin using calculable asymptotic behavior; a candidate solution can then be checked against the full positivity problem. This pass does not perform that check.

Conformal-block decomposition and crossing symmetry yield the sum rule 1=Σ c²Δ,l Fd,Δ,l. Positivity of squared OPE coefficients makes the allowed sums a convex cone; spectral restrictions remove generators, while separating linear functionals can exclude spectra or bound individual coefficients.

Uses thick-thin decomposition and the Margulis lemma to organize short-cycle regions into garters and cusps. Local Kaluza-Klein reductions on their small circles or tori provide effective descriptions with different compact topologies and potentially different effective dimensions.

Constructs the trinion using a discrete Fuchsian group free on two generators. The appendix builds a canonical Fricke fundamental polygon from isometric circles and identifies generator axes with the closed geodesic garters.

Use Weierstrass discriminants and Tate’s local coordinate algorithm to identify degeneration types and enhancement loci. For SU(5) along w=0, the Tate coefficients have vanishing orders (0,1,2,3,5) for (a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4,a_6).

Resolve singular fibers into intersecting P¹ curves, read their Cartan intersection structure, and interpret gauge states through reduction of the M-theory three-form and M2-branes wrapping shrinking cycles. Toric methods provide explicit resolutions for suitable hypersurfaces and complete intersections.

The SU(5) spectral cover is b_0s⁵+b_2s³+b_3s²+b_4s+b_5=0, compactified inside W=P(O_S⊕K_S). A spectral line bundle pushes forward to a rank-five bundle. The review states without proof χ_10=−λ∫_Sη(η−5c_1(S)), with equal net chirality for the corresponding 5 matter.

Numerically solves ∂V/∂xᴬ = 0 while varying c, singlet vevs and M_d, including searches over all ten real components. Stability is assessed through mass eigenvalues. The authors report precision checks up to 1000 digits and retaining 20 terms of the eta-function expansion.

Uses periodic axion potentials to identify candidate critical phases analytically before studying the coupled real moduli. Cosine extrema supply candidates rather than guaranteed minima; additional axionic critical points can depend on the real moduli.

Builds K, gauge kinetic functions and W from dimensional reduction and string-amplitude results. Computes explicit trilinear worldsheet-instanton sums and anomaly coefficients, and uses modular covariance, including Poisson resummation of Yukawa sums, as consistency tests.

Clock comparisons use transition-dependent relativistic sensitivity factors computed with numerical many-body methods. Quasar analyses use relativistic q-coefficients, multiple transitions and fitted absorption profiles to distinguish changes in constants from a common redshift.

Oklo inference proceeds from isotopic abundances through reaction networks and flux-averaged neutron-capture cross sections to resonance shifts and nuclear sensitivities. Meteorite isochrons instead constrain an integrated decay history, requiring independent age calibration and present laboratory decay rates.

Use a sensitivity chain from an observable O to primary parameters Gk, then to fundamental constants αi. The first stage requires a physical model of the measured system; the second depends particularly on nuclear physics and any assumed unification framework.

Use the Atiyah extension 0 → End(V) → Q → TX → 0 and its long exact cohomology sequence. For the example, compute jumping extension cohomology with a Koszul sequence and Bott–Borel–Weil polynomial representations; use Serre duality to bound the obstruction rank.

Relate the positive gauge-field contribution in the ten-dimensional action to four-dimensional F-terms using W = ∫X Ω ∧ H and the gauge Chern–Simons dependence of H. In the Minkowski vacuum W = 0, giving FCi = ∂W/∂Ci.

Linearize the Hermitian Yang–Mills equations under integrable complex-structure changes and arbitrary non-harmonic connection adjustments. The holomorphy constraint is δzᴵvᴵ_[ā]ᶜF⁽⁰⁾_|c|b̄] + 2D⁽⁰⁾_[āδA_b̄] = 0. An elliptic-equation argument is then used to satisfy the remaining trace condition.

Generalized gauge-condition-independent background-field effective action. A parameter v distinguishes the generalized construction, v=1, from the standard background-field calculation, v=0; gauge-condition parameters are retained to expose dependence in the standard result.

Proper-time regularization and a small-proper-time heat-kernel expansion identify quartic, quadratic and logarithmic divergences through E0, E1 and E2 respectively. The regulator is chosen to retain possible power divergences while respecting the stated invariances.

E1 is obtained from the pole of the coincident Green function using local momentum space and a normal-coordinate expansion. Only terms through G2 in the large-momentum expansion are needed near four dimensions; the author reports substantial Cadabra use and an alternative-method check.

Expands moduli about their vacuum values and diagonalises the kinetic/mass system to obtain canonical fields. Couplings are obtained by expanding the moduli-dependent kinetic and mass terms of open-string modes and expressing them in canonical variables. The paper imports the detailed coupling calculations from earlier work.

Combines nonperturbative superpotential terms, the leading α′ correction to the Kähler potential, and an anomalous-U(1) D-term. Comparing VD of order V^-2 with VF of order V^-3 fixes the Fayet–Iliopoulos term to zero at leading order; the remaining F-term potential stabilises the blow-ups and an exponentially large volume.

The coordinate r=R sinχ removes the areal-coordinate obstruction at the equator. Matching to charged Nariai is performed in Gaussian normal coordinates by imposing continuity of the metric and its first normal derivative, giving a linear system for exterior constants.

Under total-stress isotropy and constant effective density, the authors introduce z=ρ+p and integrate its first-order equation by separation of variables. Integration constants are fixed with central pressure/density and the time normalization e^a(0)=1, without requiring a pressure-free surface to exist.

Uses the leading diagonal Kähler metric and a field redefinition to obtain canonical kinetic terms. Evolves homogeneous fields together with the linear Newtonian-gauge metric and field perturbations, decomposing the quantum fluctuations into a matrix of mode functions ψij.

Expands the supergravity scalar potential in inverse powers of the compactification volume. The leading V^-3 contribution separates into individual inflaton potentials; the V^-4 contribution supplies a weak interfield coupling. These orders are retained for the numerical two-field analysis.

Numerically integrates the coupled background and mode equations and computes the curvature spectrum from the mode functions. A metric constraint is used as a numerical precision check. CAMB and the LAMBDA likelihood code are then used for the historical WMAP7 TT comparison.

Uses anisotropic engineering dimensions [dt] = [κ]^-z and [dx] = [κ]^-1 to count coupling dimensions. The scalar example has [φ] = [κ]^((d−z)/2); the gravitational discussion additionally accounts for spatial derivatives in self-interaction vertices.

Reviews an action-level relation to Einstein-aether gravity by imposing hypersurface orthogonality through a scalar-defined unit vector and choosing that scalar as time. Background cosmology is analysed through modified Friedmann equations, retaining the distinction between global and local Hamiltonian constraints.

Studies constraints by varying the lapse and examines quadratic perturbation actions around flat space. Canonically normalised cubic interactions estimate strong-coupling scales, with explicit attention to whether higher-spatial-derivative operators enter before the low-energy perturbative expansion fails.

Canonical quantization supplies coupled mode functions and Wronskian-type initial conditions. Independent quantum-mode labels are distinguished from field-space directions; spectra sum contributions from all quantum modes.

Gauge-invariant Mukhanov–Sasaki perturbations are projected onto moving orthonormal vielbeins. An antisymmetric connection accounts for derivative mixing; a time-dependent orthogonal rotation gives canonical kinetic terms and a generally mixed mass matrix.

The authors numerically evolve the coupled slow-roll perturbation equations through prescribed turns and a sigma-metric toy model, comparing end-of-inflation spectra with the effective equation. Initial conditions use finite-time Hankel solutions before turning begins.

Cosmological burst rates use redshift integration. The paper compares approximate interpolating functions neglecting Ω_Λ with numerical integration for its chosen concordance cosmology, presenting both amplitudes at fixed rate and rates at fixed amplitude.

The waveform calculation follows the Damour–Vilenkin Fourier-integral framework: a saddle-point expansion treats the smooth mover, while endpoint contributions around the discontinuity treat the kink mover. The far-field metric follows from linearized Einstein equations.

The authors retain the Lorentzian four-vector magnitude and denominator factors in the kink integral. Angular averages over the sphere and representative great-circle fans assess whether detailed amplitude and geometry alter the usual rate estimate.

The holographic dictionary distinguishes homogeneous leading source terms from spatially modulated subleading expectation values. A prescribed square modulation of an Abelian scalar at the wall is propagated toward the boundary using a modified-Bessel-function solution as a toy estimate.

An Abelian magnetic-bag approximation neglects lattice detail and non-Abelian fields. The interior has φ=B=0; exterior scalar and magnetic fields determine an energy whose minimization fixes the wall position. Scalar profiles for nonzero λ are obtained numerically.

Backreacted walls are constructed by numerically solving Einstein–Maxwell–scalar equations and patching the exterior to an AdS or Schwarzschild–AdS interior. In the tensionless-wall approximation, Israel matching requires continuity of C, D and C′, while D′ may jump.
Dehn-twist actions on contours are analyzed through their branch-cut phases. Linear combinations of contour images construct eigencontours for monodromies associated with a chosen pants channel.

Examples use Selberg integrals, Gamma and double-Gamma functions for three-point amplitudes, and hypergeometric differential equations plus contour-dependent boundary behavior for degenerate four-point blocks.

A quasi-conformal coordinate w = W/gs and metric |dw|² convert potential-gradient trajectories into straight lines on a light-cone string diagram. Poles and zeros of dW determine external tubes and interaction points.

Fermion supersymmetry variations give first-order scalar-gradient and warp-factor flow equations. The phase of W is matched to the SU(8) connection. A consistent two-field restriction is then integrated numerically to connect the maximally supersymmetric and new N=1 points.

Successive symmetry-invariant truncations use two SO(2) rotations and discrete transformations g1 and g2. Explicit scalar parametrizations yield the potential and a complex superpotential constructed from an A1-tensor eigenvalue; |W| governs the selected N=1 sector.

Scalar stability uses the quadratic fluctuation matrix and canonically normalized BF bounds; the authors report numerical second-derivative checks of spectra. Numerical searches minimize |Q|² using sensitivity back-propagation, while high-precision PSLQ searches propose algebraic expressions for selected numerical data.

Estimate thermalization by comparing decay/scattering rates with Hubble expansion, using imported interaction-rate classifications. Add high-temperature one-loop ideal-gas and two-loop interaction contributions, then compare their magnitudes with the zero-temperature potential.

Extract modulus couplings by expanding gauge kinetic functions, matter kinetic/Yukawa terms, and the scalar potential. Canonical normalization and on-shell fermion conditions enter the matter-coupling calculation.

Expand the scalar potential and kinetic terms around stabilized divisor volumes; obtain canonical fields χB, χS from the Kähler-metric-normalized mass eigenproblem involving one-half of K inverse times the potential Hessian.

Canonical quantization of gravitational waves in transverse-traceless gauge, followed by physical-state constraints involving positive-frequency field combinations and relations between Gaussian wave packets.

Alternating sums of massive propagators and imposed mass relations generate higher-denominator propagators. Renormalizability, super-renormalizability and finiteness are assessed through propagator behavior and power counting.
Leading vacuum stress-tensor estimates, numerical searches over graviton masses, and an order estimate of a selected four-graviton contribution to the lightest graviton's mass correction.

Compare numerical instanton actions through B=SE(instanton)−SE(false vacuum), with Γ~exp(−B/ℏ). Smoothness and asymptotic conditions differ between noncompact Minkowski/AdS instantons and compact de Sitter instantons.

Construct Euclidean O(4)-symmetric instantons by solving the radion equation and gravitational constraint on either side of the brane, matching radion derivative jumps and the Israel junction condition.

Reduce the six-dimensional metric using radion-dependent conformal factors, obtaining F^2=sum_i gi^2 Ni^2 and a radion potential with positive flux and cosmological terms and a negative internal-curvature term.

Pauli-Villars propagators add heavy principal-series fields with coefficients canceling coincident ultraviolet singularities. Extra subtractions can provide the differentiability needed for derivative couplings and field-renormalization counterterms.

An induction constructs general connected diagrams by adding vertices, including coincident-leg reductions and finite regulated tadpoles. Large-regulator-mass expansions are then taken while maintaining the contour locations that control infrared decay.

Mellin-Barnes representations express diagrams in the pairwise embedding invariants Zij. Gamma-function pole locations determine fundamental strips, and shifting contours yields bounds on large-|Zij| asymptotics.

Radial quantization and the state-operator map organize spectra. Bulk propagator boundary limits and on-shell actions with suitable boundary terms generate correlators; double-line diagram topology organizes the large-N expansion.

The D3-brane argument compares low-energy open-string gauge theory with the near-horizon black-brane description. A scaling limit removes the asymptotically flat region and decoupled closed strings, leaving the proposed dual pair.

A deliberately crude Kaluza-Klein energetic argument combines negative sphere-curvature potential with positive flux energy after an Einstein-frame rescaling. Their balance yields an AdS minimum with the stated radius scaling and an unfixed dilaton.

Constrain democratic Yukawa textures using multiplicities in inclusive production/scattering rates and unitarity below the gravity cutoff. Analyze the block neutrino spectrum and cancellations entering neutrinoless double beta decay.

Review the species bound using Hawking emission thresholds, charge recovery and energy conservation. Infer the quantum-gravity cutoff by saturating the bound and estimating the semiclassical black-hole lifetime.
Inverse reconstruction uses cosmic time or e-folding. Explicitly, without matter, ω(φ)=−2f′(φ)/κ² and V(φ)=[3f(φ)²+f′(φ)]/κ² give φ=t and H=f(t); an analogous construction identifies φ=N.

Metric variation gives modified FRW equations; vacuum constant-curvature solutions obey 2F−RF′=0. Linearizing the trace equation around a dense general-relativistic background supplies a curvature-instability diagnostic.

Auxiliary-field rewriting and the conformal transformation σ=−ln F′(A) produce an Einstein-frame scalar description. Nonlocal actions are localized through scalar constraints before their cosmology is studied.

Solve the Friedmann evolution piecewise, integrate χ_CP(t)=∫ₜ∞dt′/a(t′), and obtain causal-patch matter mass M_CP=t_c V_com(χ_CP). Hyperbolic volume growth converts the geometric cutoff into powers and exponentials of the timescales.

Factorize the unnormalized probability into a vacuum-production prior and observer count: p̃×n_obs, with n_obs=M_CP h. Here h counts observers per unit matter mass; allowing observer time to scan introduces f, the conditional probability that observers exist at that time.

Locate maxima through gradient-flow or probability-force arguments in logarithmic timescale coordinates. Then include the curvature prior and discrete-spectrum cutoff, and marginalize over vacuum and curvature times to infer the observer-time distribution.

Compute group invariants through traces of diagonal generators and Young-tableau states. The Weyl character formula and bounds involving representation dimension and A_R/D_R establish finite b ranges; iterative exclusions sharpen the numerically demanding SU(2) and SU(3) cases.

Decompose spectra into simple-factor blocks. At fixed N and integer b, solve successive finite partition problems using representation genus g_R, then C_R coefficients, and finally determine fundamental multiplicities. Combine blocks subject to mixed anomaly cancellation and the total gravitational anomaly constraint.

Embedding-space coordinates, Schwinger parameters, and harmonic/split representations of bulk propagators organize Witten-diagram calculations. Mellin-Barnes contour pinching identifies exchange and loop poles.

Stirling asymptotics and stationary-phase analysis connect large Mellin variables to a Lorentzian correlator scaling limit; angular integration of flat-space loop momenta supplies the comparison for the one-loop example.
Use the Mellin representation with explicit Γ(δij) factors and constraints Σ_{j≠i}δij=Δi. Symanzik's integral identity converts Schwinger-parameter contact integrals into Mellin amplitudes.

Numerically solve the inflaton equation and Friedmann equation, then evaluate Pζ≈H⁴/(4π²φ̇²) at horizon exit. This supplies numerical background evolution with the stated approximate perturbation prescription.
Compare the modulated spectrum with a constant-running extrapolation Pζ(k)=Pζ(k0)(k/k0)^{ns(k0)−1+(α/2)ln(k/k0)}, normalized to the same pivot observables.
Expand slow-roll estimates for ns−1≈−6ε+2η and dns/dlnk≈−24ε²+16εη−2ξ, retaining the smooth contribution and leading oscillatory corrections under a hierarchy of modulation derivatives.

Integrate out heavy directions approximately by solving ∂V/∂φ_H=0, substitute their field-dependent minima, and determine the canonical inflaton variable. Estimate the omitted heavy-field dynamics and the source produced by the light-field kinetic term separately.

Use dimensional reduction and scaling balances for flux and geometric energy. The fixed-cycle exercise employs a Gaussian flux-support ansatz and a local Taylor expansion of the axion profile; gravity-dual throat estimates relate induced charge, internal radius and four-dimensional potential energy.

Estimate inclusive scattering rates by large-N multiplicity counting and impose unitarity below the gravity cutoff. Both right-handed-neutrino scattering and Higgs-doublet scattering through the singlet sector constrain the Majorana-type couplings.

Diagonalize the structured 2N-dimensional neutrino mass matrix into degenerate multiplets and singlets, reduce their mixing with the original SM neutrino to effective states, and expand the LNV propagator sum for light and heavy masses relative to the process momentum.

Use Wilson lines and surfaces, linking phases, and defect operators defined by excising neighborhoods and imposing flux or homotopy boundary conditions. These describe possible ultraviolet objects without requiring them to be dynamical in every field theory.

Combine Hawking evaporation and entropy-bound arguments with an analysis of brane currents in FZ, R, and S supercurrent multiplets; track which currents are gauged, improved away, or explicitly violated.

Dualize the periodic Higgs phase into a two-form B, optionally dualize A into a one-form V, and take the infrared limit to obtain the BF presentation. Standard compact gauge transformations and allowed bundles remain essential.

Estimate backreaction through the fractional change of a warp-weighted internal volume. Separate induced antibrane sources into opposite-charge D3 sources and charge-neutral brane/antibrane pairs, using asymptotic throat perturbations and a cut-off AdS5×S5 model for parametric estimates.

Dimensional reduction estimates the axion kinetic term. World-volume Wess-Zumino and DBI actions, related by S-duality, give a brane potential proportional to e^{4A0}√(L⁴+gs²a²), with a factor of two for the brane/antibrane pair.

Use Hodge dualization and completion of squares for the tensor Bogomol'nyi bound. Obtain the Euclidean BPS projection from zero eigenvectors of the supersymmetry anticommutator matrix, then impose vanishing fermion variations on scalar backgrounds.

Project transition amplitudes onto prescribed axionic charge densities using functional Fourier representations. This produces boundary terms that enter both saddle equations and the nonzero instanton exponent; complex contour deformation supplies the fluctuation prescription.

For Hessian N_ij, introduce dual scalars σ_i=∂_i V. The extremal ansatz reduces their equations to Δσ_i=0. Geometrically, solutions map into totally isotropic, totally geodesic para-complex eigenspace submanifolds. Algebraic inversion to the original scalars need not be explicit.

Solve the warped higher-dimensional Einstein equations and integrate the gravitational action over extra coordinates. The resulting warped-volume integrals determine the four-dimensional Planck coefficient and cosmological term.

Separate transverse-traceless tensor fluctuations into time and extra-coordinate modes. Field redefinitions give Schrödinger-type problems, treated with Bessel and hypergeometric functions, normalizability integrals and brane matching. Bulk master-variable and projected-Weyl equations provide additional perturbative information.

Use the gauge δφ=0 on a nontrivial scalar background and an ADM decomposition, treating lapse and shift as constraint variables. Canonically normalize perturbations to estimate background-dependent strong-coupling scales.

Integrate out F·F̃ in the zero-momentum limit to obtain the axion potential, then examine the retained anomalous interaction through the gauge Chern-Simons three-form. Background equations follow from varying the lapse and scalar.

Reviews supergravity separability using f=−3MPl² exp[−K/(3MPl²)] and additive visible/hidden superpotentials. The weaker extended no-scale criterion is K̃_ab̄=exp[K̂/(3MPl²)]κ_ab̄ with F^m∂mκ_ab̄=0; eliminating moduli-mediated A terms additionally requires F^m∂mYabc=0.

Solves F-flatness for a supersymmetric AdS configuration, computes uplift-induced displacements using an inverse Hessian, and expands masses around that point. Soft terms come from derivatives of VF+Vup, with fermion masses subtracted from nonholomorphic scalar masses and kinetic normalization included.

Use the deformed ISS one-loop effective potential obtained by integrating out χ,χ̄, estimate slow-roll parameters and e-foldings, and track the relative ordering of the matter-waterfall and modulus-instability points. Scalar-potential slices illustrate the proposed histories.

First freeze φ and neglect DφW, solve DTW=0, and estimate the heavy-modulus mass for |aT|≫1. Then restore positive inflaton F-term energy and compare mT with Hinf to assess whether the modulus remains near its moving minimum.

Compatible generalized pure spinors encode the geometry. A holomorphic Poisson bivector implements Z = Ω + θ with ιβΩ = θ. Locally, Poincaré–Lelong gives θ = −(ℓs^4/π)∂w and w = ⟨S⟩log h + w0, where h defines the condensing divisor.

Dimensional reduction of the quadratic D7 fermion action supplies the flux–gaugino coupling and localized flux-duality correction. The paper separately analyzes RR Bianchi identities and field equations; D3 force matching and a second supergravity derivation determine the mobile-brane dependence of Wnp.

Use a microscopic superpotential functional retaining the complete KK tower, rather than only light moduli. Its generalized form is W = (π/ℓs^8)∫⟨Z,Ftw + i dReT⟩. Gauge-coupling dependence introduces the condensate correction Fφ = ∂φW − 2π⟨S⟩∂φα.

Uses dimensional reduction and Einstein-frame metric rescaling to motivate the scalar coupling. A phenomenological potential joins a quadratic stabilized branch to vMPl⁴{exp[γ(R^(−k)−R*^(−k))]−1}; matching slopes gives α=vkγ/R*^(k+1). The modified KKLT example supplies k=4/3.

Reviews matched spherical interior/exterior solutions and thin-shell screening. The nominal shell fraction is (φout−φin)/(6gMPlΦ); forces between two screened bodies receive the product of their factors 3∆R/R.

Evaluate the quadratic on-shell action at both boundaries to obtain a 2×2 kernel Δij. These kernels are normal derivatives of bulk–boundary propagators, equivalently double normal derivatives of the bulk Green function. Regulate at finite radial distance, renormalize source data and discard contact terms for separated insertions.

Solve the scalar Klein–Gordon equation using independent kernels K±: each has delta-function boundary data at its own regulated boundary and vanishes at the other. Fourier time modes and compact-base harmonics reduce the wormhole radial equation to generalized Legendre functions.

Specify frequency contours around normal-mode poles and evaluate correlators through residues. To test the interaction interpretation, Wick rotate, compactify Euclidean time and compare the mixed-source gravitational functional with factorization of a thermal trace for a decoupled Hamiltonian.

For equal charges, constructs the occupation distribution by selecting αJ nonzero components with a binomial factor and using θ(q²s)−1 in the contour exponent. The peak is evaluated by saddle methods or statistical sampling; low-dimensional brute-force data are used to assess the minimum-Λ estimate.

Rewrites the characteristic-function lattice count through a vertical complex contour and products of theta functions. Small-argument theta asymptotics produce the BP regime; large-argument asymptotics and a saddle approximation give an equal-charge small-distance regime. Intermediate behavior is evaluated numerically.

The reviewed hidden-sector construction uses a positive-semidefinite scalar potential proportional to |∂zŴ|². Its minima illustrate degenerate zero-energy phases with different SUSY properties, rather than deriving degeneracy for an arbitrary phenomenological supergravity model.

Estimate the second-phase strong scale using one-loop running, matching α3^(2)(MS) = α3^(1)(MS), with physical-phase thresholds at Mg and MS. The stated strong-coupling beta coefficients are −7 for the SM, −5 for Split SUSY and −3 for the MSSM; numerical scans then compare ΛSQCD^4 with the dark-energy target.

Weyl and coherent-state/Voros symbol maps, cyclic integration and twist conjugation Δθ(g)=Fθ^{-1}Δ0(g)Fθ. The symbol algebras are star-isomorphic, although their products differ even at leading order; integrated Weyl products satisfy ∫A⋆W B=∫AB.

Primordial spectra are projected through transfer functions using spherical harmonics and Wigner 3-j symbols. CMBEasy supplies spectra for likelihood comparisons restricted to diagonal, m-averaged CMB data.

Finite-temperature analysis uses Gibbs states, KMS identities, Kubo response and spectral representations. The deformed susceptibility is expressed through the imaginary part of the undeformed susceptibility.

Field excursions are evaluated using |Δφ(z)|/Mp=∫₀ᶻ√[3(1+wφ)Ωφ] dz′/(1+z′). The authors numerically evolve Ωq for NADE and coupled Hubble/dark-energy equations for interacting curved HDE, then compare excursions with n or c.

The proposed bounds follow a slow-roll quartic-potential scaling argument: identify the dark-energy density with V(φ)∼λφ⁴, use the model's inverse infrared length, and compare it with a proposed scalar WGC ultraviolet cutoff. The printed cutoff formulas contain an unresolved λ-exponent inconsistency.

Tree-level heavy-field elimination, Coleman–Weinberg estimates and dimensional power counting estimate moduli and Kaluza–Klein effects. The Kaluza–Klein analysis explicitly substitutes scale estimates for a full heat-kernel calculation. Inflaton/graviton loop safety is reviewed using approximate shift symmetry.

Hamiltonian analysis identifies the conserved four-form momentum and massive scalar. Integrating out F organizes potential corrections; a dual two-form formulation recasts the mass as a gauge coupling and constrains local higher-dimension operators.

Scalar fluctuations are expanded to quadratic order and organized by the SU(2) eigenproblem iεijk[Jj,Ψk]=ωΨi. Gauge masses follow from the quadratic gauge action and the adjoint Casimir eigenvalues j(j+1), including polarization degeneracies.

The authors count spectator states below H, estimate the maximum contributing angular-momentum label using the large-j spectrum, and insert the count into Λ=Mpl/√Ns. Slow-roll benchmark calculations then compare physical excursions, energy density and string scales with this cutoff.

The authors construct the supergravity F-term potential using KU(1)=Σa|Ta|²/VX, introduce a moduli-vev ansatz, and expand extrema in the weak hidden gauge coupling αHS. Determining the homogeneity coefficients requires solving transcendental equations and imposing positive moduli.

Soft terms are extracted from the supergravity Lagrangian at unification and evolved using one-loop matching and running. Heavy sfermions and Higgsinos are integrated out near mdec≈O(m3/2), leaving the Standard Model plus gauginos; finite weak thresholds are included.

A two-modulus numerical example is reported as a cross-check of the analytic approximation, giving geometric moduli around 10–50 and |T|²/VX around 0.3–1.1. These are example results rather than an independent verification or a universal compactification classification.

One-loop potentials from supersymmetry-breaking mass splittings generate hybrid-inflation slopes. Running-mass models use scale-dependent masses to flatten a region even when the tree-level inflaton mass is large.
Potential slow-roll analysis uses ε=(V′/V)²/2 and η=V″/V, e-fold integrals, and horizon-exit estimates R²≈V/(24π²ε), n_s−1≈−6ε+2η and r≈16ε.

Jordan-to-Einstein conformal transformation uses ĝ=Ωg, V̂=V/Ω² and a scalar field redefinition to canonical normalization. The review states that comoving curvature perturbations are conformally invariant and gives matching slow-roll observables.

Reviews cosmological phase-space and linear-perturbation analyses, exact spherical and modified TOV equations, and a curved-space Dirac-to-Schrödinger reduction followed by time-dependent perturbation theory for hydrogen decay.

Independent metric/connection variation, algebraic trace elimination, auxiliary-metric transformations, and the Brans–Dicke representation at exactly ω=−3/2; constrained 3+1 Hamiltonian analysis uses Dirac’s algorithm.

Thermal tests use partition functions, KMS periodicity, spatial clustering, and temperature response expressed through integrated connected stress-tensor insertions. The latter requires regularization and removal of temperature-independent divergences; independence of the proposed thermal constraints is not established.

OPE and conformal-partial-wave decomposition, descendant counting, and perturbative bootstrap in g=1/√c. The explicit scalar contact/exchange diagram expansions in Appendix B specialize to d=4 and AdS5.

Find common beta-function zeros and linearize the flow. A block-triangular stability matrix retains the two pure-gravity eigenvalues; the third eigenvalue determines whether α adds a free parameter to the UV critical surface.

Numerically integrate the unexpanded Einstein–Hilbert gravity subsystem, then the decoupled one-loop α equation. A shooting method brackets the NGFP2 critical trajectory between Landau-divergent and asymptotically free trajectories.
For analytic trajectories, fix λ=λ0, take ηN=B1(λ0)g and h2(α)=α. Solve the autonomous g equation, then solve the α Riccati equation using hypergeometric functions and its sub-Planckian expansion.

Illustrate holomorphy obstruction using 0→L→U→L*→0 with L=OX(−2,−1,2). Extension classes lie in H1(X,L²), which jumps from zero to dimension 18 on a 58-dimensional locus inside a 75-dimensional complex-structure space; the example obstructs 17 transverse directions.

Use the Hermitian Yang–Mills conditions: bundle holomorphy produces complex-structure restrictions associated with F-terms, while poly-stability and zero slope produce Kähler/dilaton restrictions associated with D-terms. These mechanisms are reviewed from earlier work.

Separate complex-structure stabilization perturbatively: W(P) depends only on Z, K splits into complex-structure and S,T parts, and W(P)=∂W(P)=0 at the perturbative vacuum. The authors argue that induced complex-structure shifts affect the remaining F-equations only at second order in small nonperturbative quantities.

Combine extremization equations with embedding-tensor quadratic constraints into an ideal; use Singular and the Gianni–Trager–Zacharias primary-decomposition algorithm, then solve simpler factors analytically and retain real flux solutions.
Determine supersymmetry from the gravitino mass matrix diag(κ1,κ2,κ2,κ2). Assess scalar stability using the inverse kinetic metric and the full 38-field Hessian, including SO(3) non-singlets.
Real shifts and rescalings move candidate extrema to S=T=U=i while transforming fluxes. This exchanges a field-space extremization problem for a quadratic polynomial problem in flux parameters.

Evaluate a gauge-invariant L(F,g) on the isotropic ansatz and compare the full gauge equations with the reduced Euler–Lagrange equation. Obtain the perfect-fluid stress tensor and Friedmann equations from this reduction.
Compare slow-roll predictions in the ns–r plane with historical WMAP7+BAO+H0 confidence contours, imposing sufficient inflation, displayed as Ne>50.

Decompose gauge and metric fluctuations into scalar, divergence-free vector and tensor sectors. Use linearized Einstein and gauge equations; at first order the three sectors decouple. The Letter reports five gauge-invariant scalar, three vector and two tensor modes.

Use the Borokhov–Gubser first-order reformulation of the coupled perturbation equations, solving auxiliary ξ variables before field perturbations. Solutions are expressed through integrals, with a zero-energy constraint on integration constants.
Use the Φ± equations and the conifold Green function to compare source/probe descriptions of the D3–anti-D3 force. Green-function reciprocity fixes the source normalization without assuming smearing.

Evaluate ADM energy from extrinsic curvature and renormalize by subtracting the superpotential contribution. This prescription gives zero energy to supersymmetric solutions; at linear order only ξ-dependent terms remain.
Integrate the background equations for three illustrated parameter/initial-condition sets and study phase diagrams, slow-roll entry, e-fold accumulation and the post-inflationary oscillatory regime.
Derive a reduced Lagrangian, perfect-fluid stress tensor, Friedmann equations and slow-roll relations. Estimate the e-fold count analytically in terms of initial ε and γ.

Construct gauge- and diffeomorphism-invariant scalar/vector/tensor variables; use perturbed Einstein equations, gauge constraints and second-order actions. Analyze subhorizon and superhorizon limits, employ Hankel/modified-Bessel solutions, and normalize canonical perturbations.

Estimate radiative masses through superspace effective operators containing a Higgs insertion and a supersymmetry-breaking F-term. Dimensional analysis uses the leading hidden-field case n=0 and distinguishes mediation from loop-particle scales.

Transform the Yukawa matrix to a mass basis using ATYB=D, with YY† and Y†Y determining the transformations. Track gauge and global charges of the mass eigenstates to identify forbidden light-generation mass terms.

Use the Runge Higgs basis to separate the VEV-carrying Higgs from orthogonal flavour-changing Higgses. Estimate extra-Higgs and gluino–squark loop mechanisms and compare flavour-changing interactions with neutral-meson constraints.

Polarization calibrations use either an ac drive at resonance plus a dc offset, producing a response linear in the offset, or an ac drive at half the resonance frequency, producing a quadratic response in ac amplitude. Resonance frequency, phase and decay time are monitored experimentally.

The authors derive an inhomogeneous acoustic wave equation from linearized fluid motion and mass conservation. Separation into spherical harmonics and spherical Bessel functions determines the rigid-wall spectrum; driven solutions use force-dependent boundary conditions and numerical integration.

Neutrality is inferred from intercepts of polarization-versus-dc-voltage regressions. Point uncertainties are chosen to give reduced χ² near unity. Positive- and negative-dc subsets are averaged separately, then half-summed to remove an observed sign-reversing contribution.

Add appropriately smeared higher-dimension primaries built from normal-ordered products and derivatives. Determine coefficients by canceling successive powers of an invariant commutator expansion; in AdS2 the tower is resummed into a bilocal correction.

Smear CFT two- and three-point functions and OPE terms, then use contour integration, hypergeometric functions and analytic continuation to identify logarithmic discontinuities that produce unwanted spacelike commutators.

An alternative derivation solves bulk equations perturbatively with a Green function supported in the authors' right lightcone. A diagrammatic identity decomposes a bulk Feynman propagator into a smeared bulk–boundary propagator plus iK, relating reconstruction corrections to bulk diagrams.

Compute low-energy dilaton and photon exchange contributions to distinguishable-particle scattering, then extract the nonrelativistic logarithmic potential. The potential conversion explicitly removes a factor 4m² associated with relativistic normalization.

Introduce auxiliary fields, integrate out vector matter, and use large-N saddle-point gap equations. In CP^(N−1), auxiliary propagators and the amputated four-point function provide a renormalization condition and running coupling.

Integrate out charged matter to obtain bosonic and fermionic functional determinants. Expand to quadratic order in gauge fields, evaluate loop integrals with Feynman parameters and dimensional regularization, and use gauge invariance to complete the local quadratic kernel into a Yang–Mills term.

Compactification on CP² reduces each chiral two-form to a corresponding chiral scalar. Reduction on T² relates string charges to four-dimensional electric and magnetic charges; T⁴ gives a two-dimensional lattice tensored with the unimodular intersection lattice H₂(T⁴,Z).

The elementary argument starts with compact chiral scalars: operator-product locality requires an integral lattice, while exchanging the two torus cycles through modular S requires self-duality. This is presented as a physical specialization of more general existing treatments.

Supergravity applications combine factorization of the anomaly polynomial with lattice embedding tests. For signature (1,1), the authors also examine embeddings explicitly in the odd lattice diag(1,−1) and the even lattice with off-diagonal entries 1.

Duistermaat–Heckman localization computes the classical equivariant volume; Atiyah–Bott–Lefschetz localization computes a twisted Dirac equivariant index. Collinear equilibria are critical points of a logarithmic superpotential; their signs are s(p)=−sign det M̂(p), using its constrained Hessian.

Rational invariants organize identical-particle statistics, with Möbius inversion recovering ordinary invariants. Scaling corrections are determined recursively in the number of centers. Dipole halos supply toric quantization and recursion relations for comparison with the prescription.

A twisted vacuum-groupoid algebra organizes charge composition and K/S wall-crossing factors. Riemann–Hilbert problems are separated into K-ray and S-ray parts through Yγi=gi xγi; coupled integral equations construct sections from Ω, μ and ω, with a twistor construction recovering the connection.

For class-S applications, analyze WKB curves on a spectral cover to extract BPS data. The proposed Hitchin algorithm uses the double cover λ²+φ2(z)=0, solves the integral equations iteratively at large R, and reconstructs a flat linear problem.

A single-field cubic inflection-point model, V=c0+c1φ+c3φ³+…, supplies an analytic comparison. With constant-term dominance and small coefficients, the paper uses Ne≈c0/√(c1c3), marginalizing with delta-function constraints on Ne and, separately, on scalar power. The local parameter density is approximated as constant.

Monte Carlo evolution of homogeneous Klein-Gordon and Friedmann equations for more than 7×10⁷ realizations. Truncations retain 27, 237 or 334 independent terms at Δmax=6, 7 or approximately 7.8. Comparisons use one, two and six evolving coordinates; reduced-field cases artificially freeze angular coordinates.

Linearize the Einstein equations for factorized four-dimensional transverse-traceless perturbations, Weyl-rescale the background to direct-product form, and eliminate matter-source dependence using the background Einstein equations. Maximal symmetry permits setting other field perturbations to zero at this order.

Expand on the two spheres in spherical harmonics and formulate the remaining weighted spectral problem on the strip. In the undeformed AdS5×S5 case, separation and t=tanh x reduce the equation to associated Legendre functions; endpoint normalizability selects the known spectrum.

For sphere-constant Janus modes, separate strip variables and use t=tanh x followed by s=t². Even and odd sectors reduce to Heun equations. Numerical eigenvalues are found by matching logarithmic derivatives of high-order series about s=0 and s=1 at an intermediate convergence point.

LARGE Volume stabilization combines leading α′ corrections to K with an exponential superpotential correction on the rigid divisor. Subleading string-loop corrections lift the remaining fibre direction; extended no-scale cancellation is used to keep these corrections subleading.

Dimensional reduction of D7 DBI/Chern–Simons couplings, followed by canonical normalization of R-R two-forms, gives Stückelberg masses. For the retained even-cycle sector, m²ab = ga gb MP² qaα(K0)αβ qbβ/(4π²); the equivalent canonical-form expression sums Maj Mbj.

The D-term analysis minimizes charged-matter potentials and integrates out their scalars, then studies residual volume dependence. An alternative imposes zero chiral intersections and solves homogeneous FI constraints, dynamically approaching simpler geometries.

Low-energy analyses use lepton magnetic-moment integrals, reinterpret a BABAR dimuon signature, estimate beam-dump production times the decay-window probability, and constrain neutron Yukawa forces. Atomic parity violation includes an interpolated finite-range correction K(M_X).

Compute leading changes to collider and scattering observables, including interference with Standard Model amplitudes. Neutrino-electron constraints use a neutrino/antineutrino cross-section ratio with the finite X propagator; neutrino-nucleon constraints use effective couplings and the Paschos–Wolfenstein ratio.

Diagonalize the neutral gauge kinetic and mass matrices, then express electroweak parameters through measured α, G_F and M_Z. This separates modified Standard Model neutral currents from direct physical X exchange.

Analyze RR quantization with integer H-twisted homology, using ∂H=∂+H∩ and a spectral-sequence calculation. H periods are quantized separately; the Bianchi identity relates Romans mass and source charge.

Construct the N=1 scalar potential from Kähler potential, superpotential and possible D-terms; search numerically for positive-energy stationary points by minimizing ε=G^IJ ∂I V ∂J V/(2V²). The alternative ten-dimensional universal ansatz expands fluxes in SU(3)-structure forms and torsion classes, reducing field equations to algebraic conditions.

Classify covering Lie algebras using Levi decomposition, representations of the semisimple factor on the radical, derivation conditions and Jacobi identities. Orbifold/orientifold compatibility and transformations preserving the projections then organize inequivalent metric-flux models.

Reduce the D-dimensional action over Z and perform a Weyl transformation to the (n+1)-dimensional Einstein frame. Derive an A–ψ potential and kinetic terms, including kinetic mixing, then examine the ψ potential with A held fixed.

Insert separated warped-product metrics and specified scalar/flux profiles into the Einstein and matter equations. Spatially flat cosmological ansätze reduce external evolution to scale-factor equations, while the warp factor satisfies ordinary equations in y.

Large-volume and 1/(at) expansions, Gaussian elimination of H fluctuations, and numerical comparisons of full versus frozen models test vacuum values, auxiliary fields and masses. Numerical examples use a minimal dilaton-plus-one-complex-structure toy sector with leading S₀=U₀=1 and W₀=1.

Superconformal component formalism retains auxiliary fields while solving the H scalar and auxiliary equations simultaneously. Substitution into the original Lagrangian is compared with simply freezing H at leading F-flat values; power counting estimates the omitted terms.

A multiverse state is assembled by summing N-parent-universe sectors. Tracing the baby sector and other parent universes, with the displayed 1/N! factor, exponentiates the integrated single-universe probability density.

The paper reviews the Euclidean wormhole sum, restricts bilocal operator insertions to the identity, and introduces an auxiliary λ or oscillator operators to localize the interaction. Its Lorentzian effective action is obtained by Wick rotation.

Canonical quantization uses the displayed √z-sandwiched Hamiltonian ordering. The general-energy eigenvalue equation is reduced to a second-order equation for √z φE and treated by WKB; continuum energy normalization fixes the prefactor before imposing E = 0.

Green–Schwarz anomaly cancellation uses factorization of anomaly polynomials and exchange of two-form fields. In 6D, I8 = ½ Ωαβ X4α X4β with Ω of signature (1,T). Legible constraints include H−V = 273−29T, a·a = 9−T, and proper-sign gauge kinetic terms requiring j·bi > 0.

F-theory uses Weierstrass fibrations with f and g sections of O(−4K) and O(−6K), discriminant Δ = 4f³+27g², and Kodaira singularities. In 6D, codimension-one loci encode gauge factors; codimension-two enhancements encode localized matter.

Modular invariance supplies even self-dual momentum lattices. Enhanced heterotic gauge symmetries are studied through negative root-lattice embeddings into Γ2,18; Nikulin embedding results provide sufficient tests in examples.

Model sequestered uplifting through a nonlinear Goldstino/Volkov–Akulov sector, giving V_lift=M^4 exp(2K/3) in Einstein frame. The uplift must be included explicitly when a relevant D-flat direction has mass comparable to or below m_3/2.

Use supergravity auxiliary-field identities and scalar-potential stationarity to relate modulus F-components, charged-matter F-components and D_A. Explicit examples additionally impose vanishing vacuum energy and examine local stability.

In the small- and large-R1 limits, integrate out the heavy vector multiplet using ∂K/∂V_H=0. The resulting effective Kähler interactions describe the light D-flat field; radiative examples balance their quartic potential against an anomaly-mediated quadratic term.

Use the five-dimensional reduction and the extremal-area prescription SA = Area(γA)/(4GN), requiring the surface boundary to match ∂A and the surface to be homotopic to A. Among competing extremal surfaces, select the smallest area.

Analyze two infinite strips, with finite width along x2 or z. First integrals determine surface profiles, while equal-time boundary endpoints constrain them. Subtract the ultraviolet area divergence and compare finite connected and disconnected branches as functions of strip width L.

Conductivity follows from the probe Maxwell action at zero density and the DBI action expanded to quadratic order in Ax at finite density. In Au = 0 gauge, solve Ax(u)e^(−iωt) and extract σxx = A(1)x/[−iω A(0)x] from its asymptotic AdS4 expansion.
Compute the open-string annulus, equivalently tree-level closed-string exchange, using spin-structure sums, modular transformations and Riemann identities to extract the logarithmic interaction.
Use Ext groups, divisor/intersection-curve cohomology and wavefunction triple overlaps to determine charged matter and deformation-induced masses; Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch supplies the chiral index.
Evaluate probe DBI and Chern–Simons actions in a magnetized D7 background obtained from rotated, smeared D5-branes through Buscher T-duality; expand the resulting potential at small flux density.

Project the Wetterich functional RG equation for the effective average action onto the retained operators. Its supertrace incorporates full regulated propagators and vertices, with a negative contribution for Grassmann fields.

Compute beta functions using regulator-dependent threshold functions and explicit linear regulators. Locate their zeros and linearize the coupled flow: critical exponents are minus the eigenvalues of the stability matrix.

Decompose metric fluctuations into transverse-traceless, vector, scalar and trace components. In Landau–deWitt gauge only the transverse-traceless and trace modes enter the fermionic flows; expand the functional trace through the vertices needed for four external fermions.

Reviewed network methods include velocity-dependent one-scale models with multiple tensions, Nambu–Goto junction kinematics and dynamical field-theory simulations. Different treatments assign common or species-dependent correlation lengths and velocities.

Observational techniques reviewed include CMB edge searches and correlation functions, stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds and bursts from loops, and characteristic lensing by strings and junctions.

CMB calculations use Nambu–Goto maps, Abelian-Higgs stress-energy unequal-time correlators and the unconnected segment model in CMBACT. The latter evaluates spectra for supplied scaling parameters rather than determining network evolution.

Use a WKB expansion Ψ=exp(S/ℏ), integrate ∂S along classical cycles, and represent higher-order period integrals by differential operators on classical periods. Invert quantum A-periods to obtain mirror maps before comparing B-periods.

Differentiate determinant brane insertions and combine them with matrix-model loop identities. Cancellation occurs for the two brane exponents ε1/εα; eigenvalue reparametrizations also give Virasoro constraints and a BPZ formulation.

Decompose two- and four-form potentials into external and internal components, apply orientifold eigenspace selection and examine which components couple to the wrapped brane. Warped dimensional reduction additionally requires compensators and mixed-field wave-functions.

Represent a throat (p,q) string by a D3-brane wrapped on a flux-stabilized two-cycle with electric and magnetic world-volume flux. Derive its DBI stress tensor, minimize for the tension and use the Fourier-space stress tensor to evaluate gravitational radiation.

Apply imported Ferrara–Zumino-multiplet and Kähler-form consistency arguments to FI terms and moduli stabilization. The discussion distinguishes flat-space gauging from rigid AdS supersymmetry, where Kähler transformations mix K and W.

Canonically normalise moduli, diagonalise their kinetic and mass matrices, track volume powers in gauge couplings, and estimate radiative mass shifts using Coleman-Weinberg arguments with attention to higher-dimensional thresholds.

Use flux stabilisation of the dilaton and complex structure, then the N=1 supergravity F-term potential with α′ corrections and nonperturbative superpotentials. Lift the remaining fibre direction using string loops or racetrack poly-instanton terms.

Project tensors with the Sachs-Wolfe line-of-sight formula and matter-era transfer functions; separate wall and residual continuum contributions and expand in 1−Ω0. The late-time calculation neglects dark energy.
Use Euclidean bounce/background equations and analytic continuation into the bubble, then evolve an exponential-plus-plateau potential and a steepened chaotic-inflation variant.
Review tensor quantisation through a scattering equation with UT=κφ′²/2≥0, thin-wall reflection coefficients, and Lorentzian mode evolution yielding an amplitude Hp and phase.

Compute vacuum energy and pressure with a spatial momentum cutoff, compare their quartic, quadratic and logarithmic terms, and subtract Lorentz-violating terms using local counterterms. Introduce a scale μ for logarithmic subtraction and remove the cutoff.

Dimensionally continue the energy and pressure integrals, analytically continue their convergent expressions, isolate the D=4 pole and subtract a local Lorentz-invariant counterterm. A finite nonminimal subtraction is needed to match the preferred logarithmic formula exactly.

Use four fictitious heavy Pauli–Villars scalar fields with coefficient constraints to regulate the stress tensor. The prescribed order removes the momentum cutoff first and then sends regulator masses to infinity to decouple them.

Dimensional reduction of D6 DBI–Chern–Simons actions and bulk RR kinetic terms; expansion in harmonic and proposed torsional form bases; electric–magnetic dualization; normal-coordinate expansion to linear order in D6 deformations.

Integer homology, Poincaré duality, the universal coefficient theorem and torsion linking pairings organize charges and Stückelberg couplings. Appendix C uses relative cohomology and gerbe holonomies to describe torsion invisible to ordinary de Rham cohomology.

For simultaneous S,T breaking, expand W around a proposed real vacuum and match Taylor coefficients through third order, which determine the potential Hessian. Numerical work uses Mathematica minimization and STRINGVACUA for simplification, without its algebraic-geometry algorithms.

Large-volume expansion of the scalar potential, axion extremization, and positivity tests for the t–τ Hessian are used analytically. Soft scalar masses are evaluated using supergravity F-terms and matter-field curvature.

Cosmological scalar perturbations are treated using gauge transformations, Bardeen potentials and Laplace–Beltrami eigenmodes. CMB/ISW and weak lensing connect observations to gravitational potentials and their evolution.

PPN uses a weak-field, slow-motion expansion. Post-Newtonian timelike motion requires g00 through O(4), g0i through O(3), and gij through O(2); comparing a theory's metric with the test metric yields observationally constrained parameters.
Variational formulations distinguish metric variation from independent metric/connection variation and metric-affine matter coupling; Lagrange multipliers impose selected geometric constraints.

Radial reduction and elimination of electric potentials give a one-dimensional mechanical action with V_BH = −QᵀMQ/2. A separate Hamiltonian constraint is essential for equivalence to the original field equations.
Gibbons–Hawking circle reduction and the floating-brane ansatz lead to harmonic-function descriptions for BPS configurations and bubbling equations for almost-BPS configurations.

Bogomolnyi square completion introduces a real fake superpotential satisfying V_BH = W² + 4g^{i j̄}∂ᵢW∂_{j̄}W. Construction uses duality invariants for symmetric cosets; a Hamilton–Jacobi interpretation supplies a formal existence approach.

Review boundary-condition basis vectors, modular-invariance restrictions, generalized GSO projections, and world-sheet fermion charges to explain how different SO(10)-breaking patterns produce different U(1)ζ charge signs.

Sum the gauge and gravitational triangle anomalies of the proposed spectrum, add string-compatible states to compensate the mixed SU(2) anomalies, and inspect superpotential and proton-decay operators under the surviving Abelian generator.

For F-theory, derive C4∧FA∧FA couplings using the M-theory C3∧G4∧G4 term, then reduce magnetic fluxes to BF coefficients. Split spectral-cover bundles and their first Chern classes organize the surviving U(1)X and its flux.

Reduce D6-brane Chern–Simons couplings to BF terms; dualize RR two-forms to shifting scalars; express instanton charge violation and discrete anomalies using cycle intersections and tadpole constraints.
The original calculation uses Dotsenko-type conjugate vertex representations in H₃⁺/U(1)×R: a Wakimoto β–γ system and background-charged boson, supplemented by spacelike X and timelike T bosons.

Coulomb-gas screening insertions, charge-asymmetry conditions, Wick contractions and vertex renormalization reduce the maximally violating correlator to an integral recognized as a Liouville n-point function.

The addendum instead uses identities between discrete spectrally flowed representations to replace selected flowed vertices by unflowed ones, then applies standard Wakimoto screening integrals without auxiliary X,T fields.
Setting α=α̂=0 while retaining logarithmic five-brane sources removes the two asymptotic AdS₅×S⁵ regions. Local coordinate expansions establish smooth caps homeomorphic to AdS₄×B₆, locally AdS₄×R⁶.

Flux integration and Page-charge quantization give linking numbers in terms of f(x)=2 arctan(eˣ)/π. The partition inequalities are reduced to sums whose strict positivity follows from 0<f(x)<1 at finite x.

Imported half-BPS local solutions are specified by two real harmonic functions with mixed boundary conditions. Their derivatives and dual harmonic functions determine the metric, dilaton and form-field fluxes.

Combine intrinsic stress-energy/current conservation with extrinsic embedding equations K_ab^ρ T^ab=0. Equations of state and charge responses are extracted from explicit supergravity black-brane solutions.

Stationary embeddings extremize a pressure action at fixed p-brane charge or a Gibbs-density action at fixed global potentials. Integrated actions yield global first laws; vanishing total tensional energy supplies necessary Minkowski equilibrium conditions.

Prompt decays and a continuum density of lifetimes permit analytic abundance evolution. Numerical calculations use tower eigenvalues without the asymptotic overlap approximations; effective equations of state are extracted from numerical logarithmic slopes.

KK decomposition and mass-matrix diagonalization give a transcendental eigenvalue condition and overlaps connecting the KK zero mode, mass eigenstates and brane-coupled field. These overlaps control misalignment abundances and SM couplings.

For a 2D bulk, express the effective 1D boundary symmetry as a matrix product unitary operator. Combining three operators produces an associativity phase equal to the bulk 3-cocycle. The boundary obstruction invokes a criterion attributed to Ref. 59; that reference is not independently assessed here.

Construct lattice sigma-model state sums by assigning cocycles to branched simplices. Cocycle identities generate retriangulation/coarse-graining moves preserving the fixed-point amplitude. Ground-state wavefunctions come from filling a spatial complex, and coboundary changes induce symmetric LU transformations.

Symmetric local-unitary coarse-graining and canonical tensor networks reduce the problem to pairs consisting of an SRE state and an on-site symmetry action leaving it invariant. Equivalences include suitable on-site basis changes and addition of local degrees of freedom carrying 1D representations.

Use S(U(1)^5) charge sums and arbitrary singlet insertions to identify perturbatively permitted operators. A further sectorwise cohomology bound is used to facilitate removing Higgs triplets while retaining doublets through equivariant structures and Wilson lines.
Compute line-bundle cohomology to count GUT multiplets, then obtain downstairs multiplicities from the Γ-invariant part of H^1(X,L) ⊗ R_W. The scan imposes h^1(V)=3|Γ|, h^1(V*)=0 and h^1(∧²V*)>0.
Generate integer matrices k_a^i in bounded ranges; filter for simultaneous zero slopes inside Kähler moduli space, the effective anomaly class, and Γ-equivariance so the bundle descends to X/Γ.

Track the apparent-horizon radius, area, intrinsic embedding geometry and two curvature invariants evaluated on the horizon. Apparent horizons are found with a flow method; convergence comparisons supply some reported errors.

Construct initial data using a 4+1 Cauchy decomposition and the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints. The implementation uses second-order finite differences, radial integrations, and a Newton solve with a cyclic tridiagonal algorithm.

Evolve in harmonic Cartesian coordinates with constraint damping and a cartoon symmetry reduction. The code uses fourth-order spatial differences and Runge–Kutta integration, adaptive mesh refinement, sixth-order dissipation, and excision inside the apparent horizon.

Solve classical heavy-scalar equations using the zero-momentum Lagrangian, including zero momentum for light fermions. Identify polynomial superfield constraints through Grassmann identities and their component expansions.

Construct effective actions with constrained superfields, optionally enforcing X²=XQi=0 by chiral Lagrange multipliers. Higgsino removal uses X D̄_{α̇}Hi†=0; heavy-gaugino constraints and their microscopic realization are examined separately.

Expand solutions in matter auxiliary fields relative to FX and retain terms contributing through four fermions. For general Kähler potentials, use normal coordinates, Kähler curvature and the inverse scalar mass matrix.

Reheating is studied through scalar decay vertices, chiral-fermion and gravitino couplings evaluated at the vacuum, and inflaton-dependent gauge kinetic functions. The late perturbative treatment requires a decay rate that remains nonzero as the oscillation amplitude vanishes.

The analysis uses the supergravity F-term potential, transverse scalar Hessians and an expansion of the coupled potential about S=0, ρ=σ0. Solving the expanded transverse stationarity conditions estimates displacement of the inflationary trajectory.
Scan reflexive lattice polytopes for codimension-one reflexive sections; triangulate using extended PALP, calculate ambient Mori cones, and use SINGULAR for hypersurface intersection rings.

Divisor identification uses adjunction, Chern and Todd classes, Euler characteristics, and explicit projected fans with restricted hypersurface equations. Fibration projections are tested against Stanley–Reisner ideals.

Diagonalisation searches integer divisor combinations whose volume quadratic forms have exactly one nonzero eigenvalue. A nonzero pairing of the divisor vector with that eigenvector isolates a cubic self-intersection; zero pairing produces a different intersection structure.

KK decomposition and diagonalization of the instanton-induced mass matrix yield a transcendental eigenvalue equation and normalized mixing coefficients. Interaction vertices determine partial widths; phase-space bounds and continuum approximations bound three-axion decays.

Misalignment evolution uses mX(t)=mX Θ(t−tG), decoupled damped-oscillator equations, oscillation averaging and matching across cosmological epochs. Summing constituent densities gives ensemble observables; the appendix supplies constant-mass solutions using confluent hypergeometric functions.

The density argument integrates the continuity equation and bounds the resulting integral using the monotonic comoving Hubble horizon and minimum ε. For variable cs, the conformal-time interval is related to the freezeout interval through its average sound speed.

A time transformation dy=cs dτ puts the action in unit propagation-speed form, with q=a√(2ε)/√cs and canonical variable v=Mpl qζ. The Fourier modes obey v″k+(k²−q″/q)vk=0, where primes denote y derivatives.

Expanding in ξ̂/V̂ and Ae^(−at)/|W0| reduces the single-modulus potential to a negative exponential term plus a positive inverse-power term. The allowed window is bounded by simultaneous V=V′=0 at its lower edge and V′=V″=0 at its upper edge.

Heavy-field shifts are estimated by δθ=−(V⁽⁰⁾θθ)⁻¹δV⁽¹⁾θ. The authors then estimate second-order potential corrections and volume backreaction, calculate Hessian spectra with attention to canonical normalization, and compare selected approximate and full potentials numerically.

Spectral dimension is extracted from heat-kernel return probabilities. Black-hole profiles use Fourier smearing of the source, numerical density integrals, and integration of the resulting mass function.

Ultraviolet power counting combines the assumed propagator and vertex scaling with I=V+L−1. Entire functions are constructed through an integral involving a polynomial pγ+1 and an auxiliary entire function ζ.

The author constructs a weighted harmonic-gauge action with ghosts, discusses BRST invariance, and inverts the quadratic graviton operator using spin projectors. The simplified physical propagator is discussed in the ξ=0 gauge.

Euclidean scalar-gravity instantons determine nucleation rates and initial conditions; analytic continuation supplies Lorentzian bubble geometries. Thin-wall solutions permit closed-form calculations but are not required for the underlying bubble symmetries.

Linear inflationary perturbation theory evolves a causal inflaton profile using the massless de Sitter scalar solution. Sachs-Wolfe projection estimates CMB temperature signals; detailed postinflationary evolution and disk-edge polarization require numerical treatment.

Vacuum-dominated regions are joined across thin walls using Israel matching conditions to determine domain-wall trajectories. An analytic continuation of Vaidya-type metrics motivates the new null-radiation solution.

The δN expansion expresses ζ in scalar and vector perturbations through second order. Polarization-resolved two-point functions and their tensor decomposition determine the power spectrum; the corresponding quadratic expansion supplies bispectra and f_NL.

Mode functions are quantized in left/right transverse and longitudinal polarizations, matched to subhorizon vacuum conditions including a longitudinal boost factor, and evaluated in the superhorizon limit. Bessel solutions and rapid-oscillation averages describe homogeneous evolution.

Five invariant-mass observables are fitted: the dilepton edge, dilepton–jet edge and threshold, and low/high lepton–jet edges. Piecewise endpoint formulas distinguish on-shell sleptons from three-body neutralino decays; in the latter case, endpoint positions contain no slepton-mass information.

MultiNest nested sampling computes Bayesian evidence and posteriors for linear and logarithmic priors. MINUIT minimizes χ², seeded from a high-likelihood sampled point; best-fit p-values provide a qualitative frequentist comparison.

SOFTSUSY3.1.7 predicts spectra and endpoints. Each endpoint's theory uncertainty is set to half the difference between SOFTSUSY and the ATLAS/ISAJET prediction; experimental and theory errors enter the likelihood in quadrature.
A scaling operator D=−aτ∂τ−bρ∂ρ excludes positive extrema whenever DV≥cV with c>0. This existence criterion is revisited systematically from earlier literature before adding stability constraints.

Extremum equations eliminate selected potential coefficients in favor of other coefficients and modulus values. These substitutions hold only on shell; the coefficients are not thereby promoted to functions of the universal moduli.

At an extremum, the authors examine the two-variable Hessian M and its trace and determinant. Sylvester's criterion makes positivity of this universal-modulus block necessary for positivity of the full moduli Hessian.

Tracer abundances are interpolated onto a regular Cartesian grid using qhull/qgrid3, combined with densities from the full hydrodynamic grid, and integrated as N(i,x,y)=∫nX(i,x,y,z)dz to construct face-on column maps.

The authors integrate 1,334 reactions involving 125 species using DVODE, with cubic-spline interpolation of physical histories. The network starts from UMIST Rate 95, incorporates KIDA updates, and adds thermal desorption and selected three-body reactions.

An initially Q≈1 disc is relaxed for 500 years at low azimuthal resolution, then seeded with 5% density noise and evolved for 388 years at full resolution. Mass-weighted tracer elements supply temperature and density histories for chemical calculations.
Associate a bundle to each representation ρ of H in the principal bundle G→G/H. Use A=εⁱρ(Hᵢ), with curvature F=−½ f_abⁱρ(Hᵢ)eᵃ∧eᵇ; one-dimensional representations give line-bundle building blocks.
Use reductive Lie-algebra decompositions and Maurer–Cartan equations to construct invariant metrics, SU(3)-structure forms and curvatures algebraically from structure constants.

Compute Pontryagin classes, volumes and intersection numbers using explicit curvature and generalized Gauss–Bonnet. Apply Atiyah–Singer: for a line-bundle sum with c1(V)=0, ind(V)=−⅙ d_rst Σᵢpᵢʳpᵢˢpᵢᵗ, measuring net chiral asymmetry.

Apply Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch, adjunction, Serre duality and Leray spectral sequences to indices and the E3/M5 dictionary. In the example, Poincaré-dual rigid curves impose linear constraints on divisor moduli.

Use twisted Dolbeault cohomology and Hodge decomposition to identify surviving modes as kernels of flux-dependent maps. Extrinsic curvature realizes the connecting map from divisor deformations to induced complex-structure deformations.

Wick-rotate and κ-fix the Green–Schwarz D3 fermionic action, then topologically twist fermions into differential forms. The generic-τ action is argued by SL(2,Z) covariance, including compensating κ transformations.
Postulate a differential and intersection algebra of non-harmonic two-, three- and four-forms; constrain it through partial integration and agreement with perturbative orientifold quantities.

Use local A-type singularity deformations, resolutions, K3 mirror symmetry and a chain/Stokes argument to motivate the non-closed diagonal two-form. This supplies local geometric motivation rather than a complete global construction.

Reduce eleven-dimensional supergravity to three-dimensional N=2 supergravity, dualize selected gauged scalars, and use a Legendre transformation to compare with circle reduction of a four-dimensional gauged theory.

Linearize bundle holomorphy: δzᴵvᴵ_[ā]ᶜF⁽⁰⁾_|c|b̄] + 2D⁽⁰⁾_[āδA_b̄] = 0. A complex-structure variation survives precisely when a compensating bundle-valued one-form δA exists; cohomologically this is the Atiyah-kernel condition.

The bottom-up algorithm computes jumping extension cohomology through the Koszul sequence and solves (p₀+δp)(k₀+δk)=0 near a chosen nonzero kernel element. Ambient coordinate redefinitions are removed; Bott–Borel–Weil polynomial representations permit Gröbner-basis calculations.

The four-dimensional description uses W=∫X Ω∧H with gauge Chern–Simons dependence. Near the split SU(2) bundle, W=λij(z)C+ⁱC−ʲ to lowest order; a nonzero C+ expectation value makes F-term vanishing constrain complex structure.

Rescale time as τ=ε²ᐟ³t/(gsMα′) for numerical integration. An approximate Hamilton–Jacobi calculation then treats the first descent as radial, uses N=∫(H/η̇)dη, and combines potential-dominated expansion with a near-DBI-speed-limit radial velocity.

Integrate the DBI plus Wess–Zumino brane equations together with Friedmann evolution, retaining nonlinear kinetic terms and the full radial geometry. The two dynamical internal coordinates are η and ϑ, with angular metric coefficient B(η)=½K(η)coshη.

Linearize departures from imaginary self-duality around the unperturbed throat. Since the IASD flux source enters quadratically, Φ− obeys the homogeneous six-dimensional Laplace equation at linear order. Separate its lowest one-angle harmonic on the deformed-conifold metric.
Solve asymptotic scalar and tensor mode equations; analyze curvaton Bessel solutions by sub-Hubble matching and super-Hubble expansion, then compare curvaton and background density scalings.

Eliminate H using the Friedmann constraint, obtain a second-order equation for Π, classify far-past asymptotic balances and numerically evolve candidate bouncing backgrounds. The benchmark uses F = H̄ = Mpl = 1, α = 1/3 and Π₀ = 0.

Use ADM decomposition and uniform-Π gauge, solve lapse and shift constraints, and extract the quadratic curvature action with kinetic coefficient D and sound speed squared c_s². Canonical modes use u = a√D ζ.

Use the holographic Weyl anomaly to relate curvature-squared couplings to CFT central charges a,c. At the order considered, R² and Ricci-tensor-squared terms can be removed by field redefinitions, leaving the Riemann-squared coupling in η/s.
Review the Kubo prescription η = −lim_{ω→0} Im G_R,xy,xy(ω,0)/ω. Holographically, small shear metric perturbations h_xy determine the stress-tensor retarded correlator.
Explain Einstein-gravity universality through the zero-frequency graviton absorption cross-section: absorption equals horizon area, while entropy is proportional to the same area.

Solve background gaugino and supergravity supersymmetry variations, impose spinor projections, and reduce the radial flow to first-order equations. IR scalar values follow from stationarity of an effective superpotential.

Use Landau-level spectra, uplifted D3-probe DBI and four-form couplings, and the AdS3 central-charge formula. Coulomb probes must include magnetic-plane dependence and its gradient energy; constant transverse coordinates alone are not gauge invariant.

Refine the Ashok–Douglas argument using the bounded positive quadratic form N̂·(Gτ⊗Gz)·N̂ᵀ=L≤Lmax. Period expansions determine asymptotic eigenvalues and eigenvectors; positivity and flux integrality constrain which components can survive near a D-limit.

Numerically evaluate periods, superpotentials and scalar potentials on successively refined grids. Full Meijer-function periods benchmark inexpensive LCS expansions; conifold monodromies generate successive flux configurations and branch changes are tracked.

Generalize flat Galilean shifts using covariantly constant Killing one-forms, inspect scalar equations using curvature contractions and Bianchi identities, and use existing second-order scalar-tensor classifications to restrict invariant operators.

Use ADM Hamiltonian variables to compare scalar kinetic energies. For no hair, integrate the scalar equation over the exterior region, eliminate boundary terms under stated conditions, and use the metric equations to obtain a positive bulk integrand.

Expand Einstein gravity in a scalar-gradient-dependent metric to identify an approximate Einstein-frame description. Use unitary gauge and canonical propagating variables to discuss background-dependent strong coupling.

Compute a static D2 probe's DBI plus Wess–Zumino force and calibrate boundary conditions by adding ordinary BPS D2 branes. Opposite shifts of g2 and g3 change the Maxwell D2 charge while preserving the S4 flux and reproduce the expected smeared-brane warp-factor singularity.

Reduce the IIA Ansatz to a one-dimensional sigma model, eliminate nondynamical fields, and use the superpotential attributed to Herzog, with V=(1/8)G^{ab}∂aW∂bW. The superpotential is a device for organizing the radial equations.

Apply the imported Borokhov–Gubser method: replace seven second-order equations by fourteen first-order equations for deformation modes and conjugate variables ξ, retaining the radial Einstein zero-energy constraint. The ξ subsystem closes and sources the field-deformation equations.

Analyze regular instantons through overshoot/undershoot shooting, local hypergeometric or Bessel approximations near extrema, bounds on scalar velocity, and estimates of barrier-crossing time. Numerical shooting is also used to assess whether particular potentials actually enter the thin-wall regime.

Use the trace of Einstein's equations to obtain the on-shell bulk action SE=−2κ∫√gV/(d−2). Approximate its true-vacuum, wall, and false-vacuum regions separately, then extremize the reduced action with respect to the wall radius.

The η-problem is illustrated by expanding the supergravity exponential prefactor around a canonical Kähler potential and examining slow-roll derivatives. The Lyth relation connects tensor amplitude to canonical field excursion over the observable interval.

The model-building strategy first seeks a de Sitter vacuum with all closed moduli stabilized, then searches for inflationary directions. The review derives illustrative scalar potentials from K and W and converts geometric moduli to canonically normalized inflatons.

Extended no-scale cancellation is explained through inverse-Kähler-metric expansion and homogeneity in two-cycle volumes. A Coleman–Weinberg estimate with the Kaluza–Klein scale as cutoff supplies a low-energy interpretation of loop-volume scaling.

Its central method is a critical audit of approximation domains, omitted interactions and fields, and theoretical errors. The recommended research program combines explicit moduli stabilization, naturalness analysis, heavy-field effects and well-founded expansions.

For singularities it surveys exactly solvable Lorentzian-orbifold CFTs, string quantization in exact plane waves, resolved-background limits, and AdS/CFT descriptions. These are imported tools and results concerning special backgrounds.

For low-curvature bounces, the review uses the FRW Einstein equations at vanishing expansion rate and positive acceleration to identify the necessary energy-condition violations, with a separate positive-curvature case.
